When I originally typed up this review, I had this unit less than 3 months and the paint on keys of the keyboard were peeling away. The letters are transparent so the red back lights shows through. Great, however, the surrounding paint on the keys are peeling, so you can no longer make out certain letters. This is a cheap keyboard, but I like the silly red lighting which matches the system. I mean, seriously, less than 90 days and my L key has disappeared, my space bar looks like a sketchpad, and now my left shift and S keys are going. I paid $1450, not $600.00. I don't expect an amazing keyboard, but I've never had keyboard paint on keys peel away -- even on the cheapest Logitech.

EDIT: Contacted tech support - Asus does not replace keyboards that come with a system past 30 days. They only honor the actual PC for one year. The rep tells me the seller may have not have sent you the correct keyboard and I should ask them to replace it. Imagine this BS? The keyboard is correct, the box was sealed, and the seller is well established and highly rated. They would not do something so heinous. I go back to Asus tech support using their chat system (where it feels like the rep takes lunch brakes in between replies). I explain everything from scratch, hoping I get a more understanding response to my situation. The chat support response is canned "we want to make our customers happy, blah blah blah.." After 20 minutes between of back and forth questions, he finally asks "OK, so you would like to exchange the keyboard for a new one, correct?". I of course, reply with a yes, and even if the second one has this problem, I will live with it. He tells me to hold on a few minutes more. EIGHT minutes later he returns the same response I received from my email support. We are sorry but we're unable to exchange your keyboard after 30 days. Only the PC itself is under warranty for a year.

Oh, and for those who are intentionally checking off this review as "not helpful", you are only hurting other potential buyers. From here on in, when anyone asks me what computer I would recommend, it most certainly will not be an Asus.

These are the first security cameras we've ever used, and I was able to install them myself in about a half hour. While they do a good job recording video and saving it so I can view it on my phone, the app is lacking and there are a couple of things that I find frustrating. I'll break my review into pros and cons.

Pros:
1. Fast install
2. Rechargeable (but only one base station)
3. Can view what is going on in my house when I am not there, can talk to the dog if I see him getting into the trash
4. Backs up my videos so I can look at them later if I am not home but cannot check the notification
5. I like the option to have a light come on at night, sound a siren, or call emergency services.
6. Decent video, I don't think it's 4k HD though, and wonderful audio.

Cons
1. The battery life. It lasts about 5 days, but one of mine is mounted outside so I have to stand on a chair or ladder to disconnect it and reconnect it.
2. Only one charing base is included for two cameras. They usually die around the same time and I can only charge one, the extra chargers are pricey and it seems to be a proprietary wire.
3. It came with one magnetic mount, which I love, and another mount that is a screw and ball. This mount doesn't feel as secure and I don't get why it just didn't have two of the same ones. It looks weird having the same camera with different mounts.
3. They are 4k, IF you pay. If you don't then they record in a lower quality. I don't mind, but it's misleading how it's phrased.
4. The app is clunky. I found it hard to block out areas where I didn't need notifications (like, every car that drives by on the road). I also was overwhelmed with notifications every time someone walks through my living room. I figured out how to set the cameras to a schedule/geo-fence, but WATCH OUT! The geo-fence doesn't work if you disconnect your phone from Wifi when you leave.
5. Notifications: When I'm not home I get an alert every time my cats walk through the room, so I had to shut off notifications all together. A little frustrating, but understandable.
6. Timers. If you want the camera to run from 10pm to 5am, you have to set it for the current day 10pm-11:59 pm, then the next day from 12:01am to 5:00am. It's kind of difficult and it kept not saving it when I set it up that way so I gave up and just set it from 12:01am-5:00am.

So. Yes. It’s sturdy and seems it’ll protect an iPad really well.

Unfortunately, for the past 6 years, we’ve been spoiled by an iPad mini case made by Ballistic, that isn’t made any more. So I just don’t buy “well sure it’s inconvenient and bulky but it has to be, to protect well.” It really does not.

This plastic Otterbox uses is so very rigid, the protective cover is extremely difficult to pop on and off. When kiddo’s alarm goes off and he’s already off somewhere, it takes me ages to get the thing open to shut it down. I also can’t find the power or volume buttons easily by touch, they blend in so much.

What’s outright laughable is the kickstand. It’s on the inside of the cover that you take off, so you set the iPad on it. It doesn’t sit very securely at all, and now that this model has the pencil holder, in some positions it won’t stay up - it teeter totters right over! So no, it’s not a 4 position kickstand, but a 3 position. The whole situation is anything but stable, so if there’s a tug on a charger or headphone cord, instead of just sliding a tiny bit on the table or not doing anything at all, it slips off the kickstand and ... well, this is how we already know it’s sturdy, as the thing ended up on the floor more times in the first day than the iPad did in a year in its old case.

It’s quite heavy compared to other choices that offer similar protection, and very very difficult to install. I am never need to read directions type, and these directions were meaningless. It required a YouTube and a lot of swearing, plus a sliced open cuticle, to get it on. Even then it didn’t seat properly around the speakers and needed quite a bit of poking into place with a toothpick.

I sincerely hope there will be a day when there’s another rugged iPad mini case, with a kickstand and a shell that goes over the screen. Because this just doesn’t cut it.

Where to begin? I tried to connect my Google Pixel 6 Pro via Bluetooth and I couldn't. I had some success with an iPhone 12 Pro Max. I tried to stream music from Spotify and Amazon Music and the volume was impossibly low. Finally, to add insult to injury I tried to tun in local FM stations to no avail. Don't buy this product. It's worthless.

Great sound and radio reception. Very easy to install on my '06 Subaru Forester (after I unhooked the HVAC clips). Beats the factory radio since I needed a USB for charging and playing Amazon Prime music (which sounds soooo much better than Pandora, btw).

I don't talk on the phone in the car so will most likely never use the Bluetooth feature for that, though I did hook up the microphone just in case. I did play music via Bluetooth and it's really inferior to plugging in the USB or listening to a CD.

The radio reception is great - better than the factory unit. (Note that the "power antenna" cable must be hooked up! That's not for an antenna that is powered to go up and down, that's for the power to the antenna. I made that mistake in my daughter's Subaru Impreza and she has zero radio reception.)

What I don't like about this unit: rather silly but yesterday 4 of us could not find where the CD eject button is. I had to come home and get the manual out. (It's UNDER the CD flap on the right. Whodathunk?)
The display is very very dim. I tried choosing different colors and none are bright enough to see in the daytime.
The buttons are very very small. The radio buttons are not the least bit intuitive as to the arrangement of them and with the dim display it's very hard to reach over and hit a button to change stations.

Am I happy with the purchase? Yes. Do I recommend it? Perhaps for those with young eyes and tiny fingers. When my next child gets a car I'll be putting this in it and getting myself a much larger 2-bay model with bigger buttons and brighter display.
It does sound fantastic, though!

Update: I've had it with this thing. I dealt with the dim display, impossible to push buttons (unless your fingers are tiny), poor button setup, and impossibly slow selection between tuner, CD, and the useless iheart/pandora choices - but now that I've gone from iphone to android phone it will not work with my phone via USB port. I'm required to download the Kenwood app, which would be fine, but it doesn't work with Amazon music or Spotify. So pretty much I have no choice but to use an Aux cord. Using two cords, one for charge and one for music, is ridiculous. This device will be out of there as soon as a replacement arrives.

Further comment: I do not use bluetooth for music - the quality is way too inferior to plugging in.

Two weeks after I got it I submitted return. Was on vacation the first week so really a week after first use. Picture went black, but could still hear sound.  Cancelled return when it suddenly worked again. It has done this a few more times.  If it is turned off and on several times it will work, but this is unacceptable for new TV. I wanted to like this. It had lots of great reviews on the web. But there were just too many shortcomings:
1) The battery only lasts an hour. This is pretty standard for action cameras, so I don't really ding it for that: I just bought a big external battery. However,
2) Even with essentially unlimited battery, the camera can only record 2 hours (128 minutes) on the largest memory card that it accepts. My bike rides are often longer. Well, maybe I could switch after a couple of hours, although that would be awkward. However, the first time out,
3) It just stopped recording after 30 minutes. When I noticed some time later, I restarted it. That session was 7 minutes long. I *was* using the recommended sandisk card.
4) The display is impossible to see outside. Not just in the sun, but in the shade. Not just in the shade, but with your hands cupped over it. It's really only viewable indoors.
5) I thought maybe I had done something to accidentally turn the camera off, so I tried to review the footage. On the phone, you cannot position the video to the end. Even if you manage to convince the software to point near the end, as soon as you hit play, it jumps back to 0, and the scrubber takes multiple swipes to move forward even a minute, so scrubbing to 30 minutes--let alone 2 hours--was not an option. So I installed the PC software.
6) On a relatively powerful laptop (i7-6650U), the software was virtually impossible to use. Buttons didn't respond--or took seconds to respond--the video and audio stuttered, and was frustrating overall. Oh, and *spoiler* I was nowhere near the camera or its buttons when it shut off, the road was smooth, and it wasn't that hot, so it wasn't something I did.
7) I couldn't find a way to connect the camera to my phone via bluetooth, which I read was necessary to get GPS information embedded. There's a bluetooth icon, but connection fails. I asked support, and they just pointed me back to the FAQ, which doesn't have any information on that. It may be that the camera only works over WiFi to the phone, but if so, they could have said so.

In the end, it was too much frustration, too little reliability, too many restrictions. When I'm riding, the tech has to "just work", and this didn't.

I received these as a gift from my husband awhile ago and have tried using them multiple times when mowing the lawn (failure) or going for a walk (semi-failure) or sitting absolutely still staring at my phone (success). The sound cuts out every 10 seconds when doing anything with these earbuds in and trying to listen to YouTube on my phone unless I'm sitting stationary without moving at all. If I try to walk around, it cuts out UNLESS the phone is no more than 1 foot from the earbuds themselves, i.e. in a chest pocket. But that's not always practical. If I try to mow the lawn with these in, the sound cuts out so much I have been tempted to rip them off and throw them in the mower's path. I've un-paired and re-paired, haven't changed my phone at all, so I'm not sure what the problem is, but these will go in the closet and probably ignored for another year. Very frustrating. The two stars are for the nice sleek case and the decent form factor of the buds themselves. Everything else has been aggravating!

They responded to the email, no idea what's wrong, this isn't a known problem, send our crap back to us. I sent back that, yeah, it was a known problem, read your reviews. Maybe fix the problem. So, no help from them, just getting my money back.

The wires are thicker which seems nice at first, but they just get in the way - the thinner wires of the ER6i would pretty much fall into place and not be a nuisance.

Buy the Cisco RV180 not the RV180W and save yourself $40 towards a better wireless access point for the wireless on this unit is Abysmal.

Cisco should be embarassed! I spent several hours giving the device the benefit of the doubt. Several hours later, I came to the conclusion that the poor signals and resulting disconnects were due to the fact the RV180W has a fatal design flaw as a wireless access point. I found an ancient Linksys WRT300N in a closet, flashed it with newer firmware (DD-WRT), and I was up and running within 15 mins without further issues using the same settings (channel, frequency, encryption, etc). The RV180W's signal is just too weak to be practical in a moderate size house; 1500 sq ft.

As a router and firewall, both the RV180 and RV180W shine. For the cost, they provide amazing value. If you are purchasing for the VPN fuctionality, do your research. Unless you are a network administrator, QuckVPN may be a non-start due to your ISP's gateway/router may not allow the traffic (Ports 50 & 51). Cisco IPSEC client is not supported, darn! L2TP does appear to be a viable alternative.

Edit:
I have since hit google and I am finding others experiencing similiar issues with the RV series. Relative new device, so a future firmware update may correct the problem. This assumes it isn't an integrated circuit or other hardware components. I have my doubts. In addition, I wish I had been more diligent for the other reviewer in May, Nick S., clearly identified the problem. I had initially done my research on the RV180 and changed my order in mid-processing to add the wireless as an after thought. I wish I hadn't.

Update; July 19, 2012:
If you require VPN, you may be disatisfied with the rv180. After successfully configuring the varing options, I tore it down and built a SSL VPN solution behind the device. The VPN solutions on the rv180 are either impractical, out dated, or featureless. For example, QuickVPN does not permit the most basic configurations like DNS. Worse, it assumes and does it badly.

As a router and firewall I no longer feel it is a good value, for I spent far too much of my time struggling with this ill conceived device. I am changing my rating from a 3 to 2.

Edit2:
So I am using this unit daily and have changed the score to 1 star. First, Cisco isn't give this unit the attention it really ought to based on firmware updates. Second, a firewall should not need to be powered off to apply updated, new, or deleted ACLs. This has been a reoccurring problem that cost me hours the first few times. I just poweroff the unit now whenever I make changes so not as to fight with it. Clearly a firmware bug.

Sometimes, if I went to the download folder, which I designated on this disk, I could find the downloaded file. Other times, the file was there, but I was unable to open it.
The third problem I noted was that files were corrupted. In the photos accompanying this review, there are titles of pre-released audio books. I am given a "one use only code" to be used on a special web page, and I get to download the audiobook files for free. In return, I write a comprehensive review of the narrator's performance. The files come in as a zip file. I unzip, rename, and move the file of MP3 chapters to an allocated folder so that a special app will play these MP3 files that are not formatted into an audiobook yet. After several days with this disk, I was listening to a book, and chapters were missing, and another book had corrupt files. I let the audiobook company know, and they checked their end. Their files were clean, and so it was on my end. At this point I went in digging looking at my folder on this disk and discovered that many of the batch of books designated for this new Microdisk had folders that were empty; these folders were not empty several days previous. Because these are pre-release files with copyright, and the disk still contains some intact files, I could not return the disk. I also did not want to erase the disk. I was going to have to ask for 20 of the audiobooks I had been assigned, to have a new "one use only" code sent to me(embarrassing). Another problem is that once the files have been unzipped and moved to the designated folder for the player, I cannot move the file again, or I will be unable to play the audiobook. Unfortunately, the company of this disk could not comprehend any of this. The Customer Service Representative had no idea what I was talking about, and refused to understand any of these basic ideas. This company clearly did not want to take responsibility for a defective disk.

My Roku had just given out when I saw this and thought it was would do as an interesting replacement.

As of note – this would likely work better as backseat entertainment only, though at nearly $280 – it is pricey.

That said …

PROS –

Picture Quality
Choice of Apps
Easy to Connect to internet
Connected to regular SDTV through RCA (y/r/w) cables

CONS –

🚩 NO REMOTE
🚩 Cannot personalize screen
🚩 Unable to connect to an HDTV via HDMI cable

Given the cons for me – this isn’t something I would purchase again or even recommend. And, it really hasn’t been used since I replaced my Roku (and got one for my downstairs TV).

Why?

I don’t like the idea of having to exit the app (be it Paramount, YouTube, Disney, etc) to turn the volume up or down as needed. It is a colossal time waster. Some programs or movies get loud with sound-effects, yet dialogue can be almost whisper quiet. And, if as an adult I get frustrated – I can only wonder how a child would react.

I also didn’t like not being able to customize the screen for apps I use and WANT to use. I don’t use Netflix, and don’t prefer to have photos out there so anyone can see them (thankfully I didn’t download any). As far as a clock – if I’m in the car – my radio has one, my phone even has one, and I could wear my smartwatch. The clock widget should be able to be deleted.

As far as using it temporarily while waiting to replace my Roku – this would not connect via the RCA cables to my HDTV. I tried the HDMI cable and got an error message that it wasn’t compatible with my TV.

The HDTV is the newest TV in the house (all right it was purchased October 2009), but the next newest was purchased in 2007.

That said … for the money … think before you get it. There might be other ways of entertaining the backseat folks on the road. As far as home use – I’d save the money and get a Roku or two.

UPDATE: The reason a remote is essential; is due to who might be viewing this in the backseat.

While the vehicle is in motion, it is dangerous for an adult to lean forward to constantly adjust the volume or explore apps.

Some people, especially kids, do not sit that close to the backseat. It’s actually unsafe to do so as a collision can cause injury or death to both the backseat passenger and the front seat passenger as well.

In addition, sitting close to the unit during a collision might cause injury from the unit itself.

As many of these devices are targeted for kids, it is even more dangerous for them to lean forward to adjust it while a vehicle is in motion. Some are also restrained by a car seat or booster seat and cannot adjust it. While phone screen-mirroring is a feature, some single parents don’t have a second adult in the vehicle to assist with that.

Also, disabled people in the backseat might not be able to adjust/navigate the unit without a remote. Even using phone mirroring can be challenging as opposed to a remote much like a TV, DVD player, cable box, etc.

For at home use – I sit too far away to constantly jump up and down to adjust the volume and/or navigate apps. I might also have it on for background noise during chores, and don’t want to have to stop what I’m doing to turn down the volume so as not to disturb the neighbors.

I thought I’d update for those wondering why a remote might be a safe, if not essential accessory to have.

Backing up files is always a good idea – whether to a cloud drive or a physical drive.

These are a fairly good deal for storage. All five (5) are 64GB.

They are a bit on the flimsy side, but still work. I did “format” them prior to use as I didn’t want any issues down the road. This has always worked for me.

The downside? They do “write” rather slow. Huge files or huge amounts of files seemingly take forever. I did them in small batches as I was backing up social media photos. That helps clear up my more reliable drives for the important things.

The “recall” time for opening files is quick.

They do come in a storage box with five “key rings” to put on a key ring or hang up. The drives come with “label” sheets to attach so you have an idea of what is on the drive.

I also LOVE the idea that they have a “cap” to them. Many USB drives have a slide cover that after a while no longer covers the USB port.

Since I’m using these for social media stuff, reliability isn’t important since I can re-download my stuff if it is lost.

UPDATE: Four months after writing this review (4/30/2021) ... I've had to toss two of these flash drives as my photos are "corrupt" and cannot be read. When I transferred the files in October, it was for safe keeping, and since they were social media pictures that I watermark, no big deal. But, for a birthday present, I received a laptop - as a result - transferring files.

Some photos are a SINGLE color (purple, blue, red), others have that old TV distortion pattern. Some folders cannot be opened due to the corruption. I opened the files shortly after being transferred - they were fine. But, these are obviously not meant for long term storage.

I'm definitely breaking these (after formatting them to erase them) and throwing them away. I will pay the money for SanDisk, PNY, or something far more reliable.

Edit: I’ve taken 2 more stars away, these can be staticky and they freeze my phone. This only happens with the buds with sensors. Super annoying.

These ear buds have the best battery power. I've been using them all week without having to charge the charger they come in. I just put them back and they are recharged. I'm not sure how many hours as it is hard to keep track of in use time. But I use them every day for hours at a time and I still get a full charge each morning.
Now the downside to these is the sensor for controlling them. This is similar to other ear buds I have with a sensor instead of a button so it is not just this brand. They are very sensitive at times and just adjusting them or tucking your hair behind your ear will end a call. You need to tap twice for pause/play and I find that I have to keep repeating it or it pauses and plays again so fast because of the sensitivity. They are mostly fine for music or audio books but I'm not thrilled about using them for phone calls. Sometimes I accidentally hang up when trying to answer a call. I prefer to have a button for better control and so I don't look weird tapping at my ear all the time.
They do fit quite well and don't bother my ears at all.

These JVC Bluetooth earbuds all have the same issues. The sound is pretty good but the controls kind of suck. The + and - button are both for volume and for skipping through tracks. But it is a guess as to whether you are going to get one or the other. Holding down the buttons should skip back or forward a song. Sometimes it does and sometimes it cranks the volume. My last JVC buds died after a few months. These seem to be the exact same so I have little expectations that these will last.

I have a pair of Bluetooth headphones of similar design but the main button for power/play/answer calls is on the side and much bigger than on this. I didn’t realize the convenience until I tried this pair. It has three small buttons that are difficult to navigate. Plus, when I paused music, the button doesn’t work to have it play again so I can only start it again from my iPhone. The sound quality is okay, not great for phone use.  They do fit really well and don’t fall off my ears.
Could not sync it to my smart remote and it would not adjust with the tv volume, even when connected properly. I was unable to use.

The RioBuds Wireless Earbuds are just okay.

The Active Noise Cancelling doesn’t work very well. I have music playing in the earbuds, the television is on in the next room, and I can hear every word of the show. The television isn’t blaring, it’s at a normal volume. ANC is one of the most important features for me with any headphones I use. Too much background noise bothers me, so it’s disappointing the ANC doesn’t actually work with this set.

The sound quality isn’t great, isn’t horrible. Music doesn’t sound like it’s playing through a tin can, but it doesn’t hit all the tones I hear with better pairs of headphones.

I don’t like the touch controls on the earbuds. I’m always bumping them when I try to put the earbuds in or adjust how they sit in my ears.

On the plus side, you can use one or both earbuds. The earbuds charge wirelessly in their case, and I like that the case has 4 LED indicators to show battery life. The LEDs also show if the earbuds are being charged inside the case, which is a feature I haven’t seen before.

I don’t consider myself an audiophile. Most of the time I can’t hear a difference between headphones. But when I put on these headphones from Targeal, I immediately noticed the lack of sound quality.

Audio played through these headphones sounds like it’s coming from far away. And whenever music or audio is playing, there’s a stuttering sound in the background. The stuttering sound pauses a few seconds after I pause the audio, but starts right back up when I hit play again. The background noise is incredibly annoying to my ears.

I had my mom try the headphones too; she’s even less of an audiophile than I am. She immediately picked up on the distant sound and the background noise, without me mentioning them to her.

The headphones have a plastic build feeling, and though they are lightweight, they aren’t super comfortable. The ear cushions on these are small, making them closer to on ear headphones rather than over ear. TARGEAL is emblazoned in silver print on both sides.

The headphones have physical buttons which is a plus: power/pairing, volume up, and volume down. They play an audio cue when powering on, connecting, and powering off. The cue is *loud* no matter what volume I set the headphones at. Fortunately pairing is easy; the instruction manual has the smallest text size I’ve ever seen in a manual.

The headphones charge via micro USB. A cable is included and so is an audio cable if you want to use the headphones in wired mode.

I honestly can’t think of an intended user for this laptop. It’s so sluggish that if I gave it to a kid, I can’t imagine them having the patience to wait for the *browser* to open. Let alone go to a website.

I’m a semi-patient adult in my 30s and wanted to chuck this laptop against the wall because the initial setup took so long. For an example, I tried to load the system information to find hardware information, and it took SEVEN seconds to open the Start Menu and load System Information.

The processor is an Intel(R) Celeron(R) CPU N3350 @ 1.10GHz. The laptop has 4GBs of RAM.

My three-year-old phone has 4GB of RAM and is snappier than the EVOO laptop. I have a Chromebook (Acer R11) that is also about three years old, and it’s snappier, too.

Windows 10 S is the default on the laptop, which doesn’t allow you to install any programs not from the Microsoft app store. I suppose that’s useful for basic users, but if you want to put another browser on, you have to disable S mode. Once you disable S mode, you can’t go back to it.

I thought I’d use this laptop for writing, since it’s so slow to load anything that I wouldn’t be tempted to go online. But I don’t even like typing on it; the keyboard feels like I’m typing on a cardboard box. There’s a hollow plastic sound when I type; it’s *that* flimsy. There are some keyboard shortcuts, but I thought it was odd that there wasn’t a shortcut to adjust the brightness. Considering how long it takes the Start Menu to load, that doesn’t make it easy to change the brightness of the screen.

The trackpad is decent, probably the best part of the laptop for me. It has a slightly sandy texture. For an inexpensive laptop, the trackpad isn’t bad.

The laptop is made in China.

I wear headphones when I work outside, spring through fall. By the end of fall, that year’s pair is pretty nasty from hours of daily use and me sweating in them. Of course I clean them, but it’s impossible to *really* deep clean headphones.

So that’s what drew me to the adidas RPT-01 Sport Headphones: the description advertises “removable, washable knitted ear cushions.” Knit covers I can wash? Hooray!

But there’s no instructions in the box on how to remove the ear covers or the headband. It turns out the cushions aren’t as removable as advertised.The ear cups twist off the headphones (a gentle, counter-clockwise turn), but there’s still an inner plastic rim. I thought I’d be able to wash the knitted cover itself, but nope. And I nearly tore the cover trying to figure out how to remove it, until I found the manual online.

I can’t figure out how to get the headband all the way off. The black plastic lining is removable, allowing the headband to be pushed up. I worry the headband will tear quickly, as the holes that line up with the black plastic lining aren’t reinforced.

Sound quality is okay … as long as I don’t use the Control Knob.

The Control Knob is like a volume rocker and skip/go back button in one. But when I used it to change the volume and skip tracks, I had static that lasted for several seconds.

There is an adidas Headphones app, but I thought it was useless. The only advantage of the app is that it allows you to set up to 3 customizable actions for the other button on the headphones. Oddly enough, at the time of writing this review, the app was only available on Android. I wanted to test the headphones on an iPhone too, but could not because the adidas Headphones app wasn’t available in my country (USA).

Lastly, the headphones are so uncomfortable to wear that I can’t wear them for more than 10 minutes. If I were inclined to use them, which I’m not, mainly because of the static whenever I use the Control Knob. I have a small head, but these headphones are tight and squeeze my ears and head. The ear cushions are actually quite scratchy too.

I live on a farm, so I spend a lot of time outside doing various things. I usually wear a pair of Skullcandy Hesh headphones, but I’m worried that constantly sweating will mean I’ll be replacing them regularly. So I was excited to check out Outdoor Tech’s Orcas, both because they are wireless and because they fit inside the ear. Less sweat all over everything, yay!

Unfortunately, the Orcas were horribly uncomfortable for me. I have small ears, so even the smallest ear tips (there are 3 sizes) were too big. It hurt to have them in for even 5 minutes. I tried them out while doing something that didn’t involve a lot of movement — weeding — and even then they kept falling out of my ears. I had to keep taking my gloves off and forcing them back in my ears. So I can’t imagine how they would stay in for anything more active. The “ear fins” are a neat idea, but again, both pairs are too big for me. I squished them in, but one shake of my head dislodged them.

Another note for the ear fins — if you have any piercings inside your ears, such as a rook or a forward helix, they won’t fit.

I did have trouble pairing the earbuds with my phone, but after tweeting to Outdoor Tech, they set me up with tech support and I had a reply within 10 minutes. (Email is support@outdoortech.com).

The sound quality was okay, nothing super great.

My main issue with the earbuds is just that they’re so uncomfortable! If you have small ears or problems wearing this type of headphones, I’d skip them. I’ll be sticking to my Skullcandys.

I haven't touched over the air television in 20 years, so I wasn't sure what to expect. The image is jittery and pixelated. Often it freezes. The sound suddenly cuts out for 20-30 seconds at a shot. I turn the antenna one way for some channels and a different way for others. I thought it might be the antenna, or the position, so I plugged it straight into my TV, and the image was very good. Not as good as cable or fiber, but good. I plugged it back into this DVR, and the image went back to pixelating and freezing.

For Internet based streaming, this device falls shy of just about everything else on the market. I could not get my VuDu account to register. The Netflix app crashed -- and let's face it, Netflix is installed on everything that has a screen and an Internet connection. The interface is so establishes, and so well understood, there is no excuse for it not to work. Hulu fared better, but not by much. For sake of testing, I swapped the Ethernet cable from my Roku, which never gives me trouble, just to rule out connection problems. It did not help.

As a DVR, it works. I can get it to record and play back with no problem. It just can't work with the antenna well enough to record anything in a quality worth watching.

The was a REGRET. Didn't have many reviews on sound quality so I took a chance. For the record, the sound quality is poor. I figured because of the brand name it might have some oompf. It does not. No base. Actually DOES remind me of an old radio. I thought it would be more like a cool speaker in an old radio base. Not happy at all with how this sounds.

Plus, the dials are hard to read. All the lines and markings are the same color as the background. You have to turn on a light to see anything. The instructions are teeny tiny too. I haven't regretted the use of my tax value in a long time but this is an absolute regret of a choice.

It is cool to look at, that is about it.

So far, I love the extended battery life, the crisp camera images, and all of the things I selected this phone for.
I thought I didn't care one way or another about the curved screen, now I'll never go back. It's elegant and upscale.
The problem is the pre-installed Gorilla Glass.
You can't put a screen protector over it, and after 2 days I thought there was a tiny hair on the screen.

I can't tell you how disappointed I am. With just minor use, the gorilla Glass is so scratched up that I don't really enjoy watching anything on my phone anymore. It's that bad. I was super excited to test this product as I use Dragon NaturallySpeaking 12 constantly, and thought that the way this model is supposed to transcribe notes into a document using Dragon would be super helpful for narrating blog posts when on the go. However, I was unhappy to discover that Dragon Premium, the next model up from my Home edition, is required to use this functionality. The new model seems to work as expected for normal recording of telephone interviews using my in-ear headphone, or for recording my own verbal notes. It does use batteries faster than my older model, even when doing the exact same task (recording audio, no fancy menu or wifi use).

Yikes, this did not work for my Wii. The way it looked on my screen was a MESS—absolutely awful, and nothing like how it looked on the older TV. I’ve tested hundreds of products, and it’s not often they arrive broken out of the box, but this one sure did, and I saw some other reviews with the same issue. These are cheap and unreliable. They look awesome and are basically a toy. You get what you pay for, but not even that in this case. I expected tinny not awesome speakers, but I thought they would at least work. Nope. Not with the headphone jack, and not with the USB. Do Not Buy.

Classic “you get what you pay for” moment here. The sound quality is pretty awful. Yes, it works fine for phone calls, and you can hear and be heard ok (not great, but ok), and pairing is easy. That’s about it. You can’t listen to music or anything else without being quickly annoyed at the internal rattle from the abysmal speaker system. It’s vastly worse than using your speakerphone. Also, the clip is so narrow that it didn’t work for anywhere in my car. Literally no place. So best case scenario, it can sit in my lap or cup holder, both of which are bad choices. Nope. Not great.

If you take the insulated thermos/bottle, detach it from the speaker, and throw the speaker out, you'd have a great product at an insanely high price. And that's basically where you are with this: the bottle does its job perfectly, offering a drink that stays hot or cold for hours, with a loop at the top to hang it or carry it conveniently with a carabiner. Everything in that department is fine, until you add the speaker.

Ease of use: great for both halves. Fits most standard cup holders, has the loop, unscrews from speaker to make it washable and versatile for when you don't want horrible sound shooting out the bottom half.

Appearance: really cool! It's a great concept, and you're probably less likely to have this speaker stolen because it looks like a regular drinking bottle from afar. Nice for the beach (partly because ambient noise makes the sound quality tolerable).

Sound quality: the worst. It's like $5 earbuds, but much louder. It is extremely tinny, whether attached or detached from the bottle, with incredibly weak bass that is almost inaudible, and shrill treble. The low and high ends come together to create a perfect cacophony of undefined sounds making every genre of music sound awful. Like iTunes played on your speaker phone, your music will sound the same but louder.

Value: I'd pay $15-$20 max for this. The sound quality really ruins what was a cool concept.

The clarity and volume are great, the construction is solid, and I love that there is an optional disposable battery backup for when you are out and about without electricity. Having said that, the range is nowhere Near what it claims to be.

We tested it in our neighborhood in South Florida, which is notoriously flat and doesn't have many thick trees or anything. Also, there's a huge lake in the middle of the neighborhood, so basically, there are almost no obstructions. Even so, it only had a half mile range. Just a few houses, big open lake, flat land.

So just bear that in mind before purchasing, in case you need range. For short distances, it is excellent.

Since this review, I have tried several times to use this with bluetooth, plugging it into the wall outlet and Trying to set it up using bluetooth. It didn't work. I use bluetooth devices on this phone ALL THE TIME. I am not a stranger to them, and I know how to make them work. For this, I went all over the site to troubleshoot, and it Never worked. The phone said it was not on or properly set up, and it never worked. I had to use a wire. Awful product. This also meant I could NOT use the calling feature either. No speakerphone.

This one gets a mixed review for the overall sound quality, but it does have some interesting features that make it adaptable and very useful. I will be reviewing its various features individually so you can better assess if this meets your needs or not. I used a decibel measuring app on my phone to determine when the speakers began to distort some of what I played.

Playing audio with Bluetooth or via USB with a computer:
-There is no noticeable difference with playback using Bluetooth versus USB, and it has a Very long range (I walked about 20ft away and it was still doing fine)

AUDIO

75 DECIBELS AND UNDER:
Almost all audio was fine: clear, undistorted, and with pretty good clarity (don't expect GREAT quality or clarity. Just Good.) Some types of music fared poorly even at this relatively soft volume. I used "Fortuna from Carmina Burana" to test the system's limits. (YouTube the piece if you want to know which song I refer to--you'll recognize it immediately) The chorus of singers sounded distorted. At higher volumes, even as lot as 85db, it was awful. Other types of music were fine (orchestra music, pop, hip hop, electronica), but sometimes the treble was a bit fuzzy.

75-85 DECIBELS:
This is the maximum volume the speakers can reach with the USB connection, so it can get loud enough for a small-medium party, but not Very loud.
It's hit and miss here. The treble and bass have some problems, especially treble. The clarity diminishes and any nuances in your music will generally get a bit lost or muffled. Choral music, music with higher pitched percussive elements, and some types of rock and orchestra music don't sound very good.

PHONE CALLS:
The voice of the person you are calling sounds a bit muffled--definitely not as good as headphones or the phone, but about on par with other Bluetooth systems I've tried.

The voice of the speaker (i.e. You) is actually clear! This part gets a solid review. With my built-in car Bluetooth system, as well as detachable ones I've reviewed, usually the person you are calling has trouble hearing you and can experience interference. Maybe that is because it is in the car and there's road noise, but in any case, the fact this one does, actually, sound clear to the recipient of your phone call is a big plus.

Overall, this is a good product when you compare it to other desktop laptop speakers. If you are comparing it to products specifically meant for enjoying audio, however, I would recommend the Pioneer Electronics Audition Series. The price is almost the same, and while it doesn't have Bluetooth unless you buy the attachment separately and it only docks with the older iPhone and iPods, the sound quality of that one is stunning. If you want extra features like FREE Bluetooth and speakerphone capability, this one is ok for the price.

I am dealing with what they call cervical tinnitus. During a routine dental procedure the doctor damaged my cervical spine muscles and the muscles at the base of my skull. So the damage muscles are manifesting noises through my neck and up to my ears. It used to be a 10 out of 10 but I’m down to about 3 out of 10. But that high whine every night absolutely precludes good sleep.

I was so excited to get this product. The set up was easy and I fell asleep right away… But about 3 hours later I awoke to electronic blow back noises. I woke up in distress because I thought it had actually made the tinnitus volume in my ear louder. But once I turned it off… It was evident the blow back noise was coming from the speaker itself. Thank God.

Cervical tinnitus vs. hearing loss or ear damage tinnitus works in different ways … and I am certain this product works for many people…I am just posting my individual experience. I’m returning it and I pulled the trigger for the $99 pillow speaker which is the size of an iPad which is placed between your pillowcase and your pillow.

I was very disappointed after reading so many positive reviews.

This unit was to be primarily used in my bathroom with my Iphone 6 while I get ready for work. It was to replace a JBL Charge I'd had for a few years and no longer would hold a charge.

The sound is strong, but tinny. No real depth or strong bass notes. I played several songs and really, really wanted it to work. Finally, I just gave up.

Now, the reason I gave it 2 stars is that it would be perfect for spoken-word use. It paired up fairly quick and the size is simply perfect for portability. And it is very attractive.

So I decided to give the Angle 3 Plus a shot for $7.00 more. Wow - what a difference! Sounds great, bass is perfect for the size, and I couldn't be happier.

Bottom line is that the choice is totally subjective on the part of the listener but, for the money, the Cambridge Angle 3 Plus is the way to go.

I have to say that this is an adorable, compact speaker. Unfortunately, it didn't do justice to the music. Some people might say that due to the size, perhaps my expectations for good sound might've been a little high. Not true because I wound up buying a JBL Charger (a little pricier) which is just a bit bigger than this unit - but worlds away in output, especially the bass.

The Rokono is excellent for transporting (backpack, purse, etc), since when it is closed up it can comfortably fit in the palm of your hand. I'm sure there are many applications a speaker like this can be perfect for - it just didn't work out for mine.

I was very excited to have a large speaker with bluetooth capability for my Iphone to use outside by the pool. This speaker was a total dissapointment on all levels. Or maybe I just received a lemon.

I thoroughly read the instruction manual - twice - to be certain I was doing everything correctly. When I was finally able to get the bluetooth to work (after having to hold down the button on the speaker until the blue light flashed multiple times, which let me know it was activated), it did work from various locations in my yard without any failures. However, as soon as I would turn off the speaker or my Iphone - I would need to re-initialize the bluetooth as if I were logging in for the very first time. The speaker failed to remember by device and so I'd begin the pressing down of the button, blue lights flashing procedure all over again. Every single time.

So I thought I'd contact the manufacturer/vendor to see if there was anything beyond their "trouble shooting" section of the manual that I might be neglecting. I looked everywhere - the box, the manual, the speaker, everywhere - no contact information whatsoever. Not an email address, phone number, snail mail or Facebook/Twitter address to be found. You buy it - you're stuck with it. The only saving grace is Amazon if you need to return it within the acceptable time frame. But what do you do if you have a problem 6 months down the line?

I installed the batteries, tried out the a/c adapter cord, and even used the 3.5 speaker cable to attach my Iphone and by-pass the bluetooth completely. I just wanted to make sure all of these items would work. But the person who designed this unit must have been having a wonderful time when they decided that in order to plug in anything at all, you need to open the battery compartment door in order to get to the connectors. This is insane and is in no way convenient. To constantly have to remove a door, or have cords hanging needlessly is ridiculous.

The sound quality is acceptable but at the price they're selling it for, you could do far better finding a speaker that has much more to offer. And if you're looking for customer service - keep looking cause it isn't here.

I really wanted to like this product, but it just didn't work out.

First of all, you need to have a really good, smooth, white surface (preferably a dedicated movie screen) to achieve the optimum results. A very, very dark room would also help. Yes, of course you could use the wall, a bed sheet or some other improvised backdrop, but it would defeat the whole point of seeing a film in the manner this projector was designed for.

Also, you must put up a credit card in order to use any of the channels available to you. Even if you are only accessing the free channels. And between you and me, I'm not that excited watching the NASA channel nonstop. You could use your Prime membership to watch movies, but that wasn't so great either.

Other reviewers have suggested it would be terrific for a slumber party. Really? What's the matter with your big screen T.V.? The picture quality is excellent but the sound is not up to par. If you're gonna go this far then you really need to be firing on all cylinders with the sound and the picture.

In conclusion, this is really a disappointment. I had hoped I could watch baseball or something else of interest to me, but this projector requires too many variables to line up perfectly, and it's just not worth the time or the effort.

The one positive - it's really cute and small.

Not what I expected and very disappointed. First day I had it I had to reset it because I had a red screen and could not get rid of it. Sound is bad. There is not enough storage. I really regret buying this and am going to try to return it!

This was purchased as a gift. I, the writer of this review, am the recipient of the gift. After about a year of "monkeying around" with this piece of technology, I have unplugged it and relegated it to a drawer. It simply doesn't work consistently. It often " has trouble connecting to the internet", even though nothing has changed. It often gets the voice commands wrong, or just doesn't respond. When it is working, (we use it mostly to stream music to a sound bar that I bought just to use with the dot by Blue tooth connection), it will often just quit, or pause and restart. I have had several conversations with the help desk at Amazon, and although very pleasant, the solution always seems to be the same. Turn it off and reinstall it. Not doing that any more. The WiFi is one room away, and lap tops, tablets and smart phones all work just fine in this room and others through out the house. It is sad, because this seemed like a great solution to get some music into this room without blasting it from several rooms away, but alas, it is a bust. Some of the things that it did, like the "this day in history" were fun, or the jokes she would tell were so silly that they were just funny, but that doesn't make the Dot worth the time, effort, or money. Save your money and buy a Blue tooth speaker for your phone. You'll be glad you did.

The music actually sounded like it was being played through a pillow, the sound was so muffled. Everything started off nice. It was easy to charge, easy to load music. I was so happy as I went walking in the water to music that I picked instead of the noise the gym plays, the sound of the hot tub and people talking. One half hour later - Nothing. Dead. I hadn't even gone under water.  Took it home, tried to charge it and nothing. Pressed and held the reset button and got a blinking blue light, so I plugged it back in to charge it. Hours later and it is still dead. I'll be asking for a replacement, and if that one doesn't work, a refund.

I got these for $40 at my local Best Buy and they are objectively pretty terrible compared to my previous $32 Sennheiser CX~s earbuds. The shiny material seems so much flimsier, almost as light as plastic, and the skullcandy logo is poorly integrated and a bit cheesy. The sound quality is tinny and poor -- it doesn't really exclude sound and doesn't give you as much of a surround feeling with lush deep notes. I feel like I'm practically listening to apple earbuds (except that they're a bit more comfortable). I'm afraid to yank too hard on it in case of compromising the inexpensive materials it's made of, and when I slide on a couch or something I get a lot of feedback from the earphones. Also, when I just plug it into the computer I hear a constant low buzz.

tl;dr not very good, even for the current $25 price. I'd spend an extra $10-20 to get something that sounds really good, and might last.

Then it stopped working after a week: to be more precise, it would play music with a significant distortion, like a piano badly out of tune. I tried various things with the sound settings and subwoofer, but nothing changed the problem.
My analysis: lots of engineering went into this, but not much quality control.

Forces me to watch AMAZON Prime VIDEO and Alexa keeps popping up. I can not access the books that I have purchase. I've spent over $100 for books and can't even read them. Not to mention the $200 for the Fire reader. Looks like electronic waste. No help from Amazon, ever.

I wanted to like it soooo bad! Because I wanted to eventually buy the T10i. But only after 2 days & less than 30 songs maybe, the volume control stopped working!?!?

They are BEAUTIFUL looking IE's. It's like the "Apple" of IE's I love the thicker cables the brushed metal 3.5MM collar the middle metal color that separates the single line to double line the over ear design. The fit in my ear was no less than perfect but C'MON guys make sure the product actually works!!!

All fluff & beauty & poor quality! What a shame!! Well, guess i'll go back to Sennheiser, at least I know their products will work over YEARS NOT HOURS!

I purchased this to use in the gym with my iPod shuffle to avoid using wired earbuds.  In the sense that it eliminated the wires, it was a success, but in terms of musical fidelity and blocking out extraneous sound, it was a failure.  Back to my earbuds.

After about ten minutes it loses the radio station signal and goes to static white noise. It's basically brand new. Another reviewer mentioned this issue and I didn't believe it. It would be great if I wanted to talk to ghosts, but I bought it to listen to the Broncos get their butts kicked. Go Hawks!
Left earbud doesn't work, only crackling and static. This is the first product I've ever had to return. Unfortunately, it seems to be a common problem, so I'm not going to bother exchanging them.

Sound is great. Ergonomics not so much. Relatively heavy ear pieces expected to stay in place based on some assumed universal ear anatomy. If for instance you try to run with them, prepare to continually fidget with them as you try to keep them jammed in your ears.

The Aiyima is overhyped. It's not a "giant killer". Its sound is pretty nice, but it clips too often. It clips into my desktop speakers, and it even clips using it as a preamp into another amplifier. Since clipping can damage the speakers, this makes the Aiyima essentialy unusable for me.

If you're not famliar with what clipping sounds like, it's a sort of crinkly distortion that almost sounds like your midrange woofer might be broken or coming detached. It happens when your unit is overworked and can't produce the full audio sine waves.

Clipping is especially disappointing since Aiyima rates the amp as 100 W or whatever, which is clearly false. My 30W desktop amp has never clipped with this system, but then it's from a reputable vendor, Denon.

I wanted to like this amp, but clipping is a dealkiller since it can damage the speakers. Not worth the risk unless your speakers are so cheap you don't care.

I paid about $340 for a refurbished unit from the manufacturer, fulfilled by Amazon. This is one seriously overrated product, based on careful listening I did comparing these against AKG K702 and Sennheiser HD600 and Denon AHD2000. I would prefer all of these against the Audeze EL-8, though the EL-8's were more expensive than all of them at even the $340 refurbished price. The EL-8's are certainly not awful, but they sounded a bit dull and veiled, and their sound stage was quite narrow, very close to head. Hard to see how these were $700 headphones when they came out. One review compared these to the Audeze LCD-X, saying you get a lot of the sound of the X for just a fraction of the price. Nope. I also compared these to a friend's LCD-X (same music, same system), and I would take it the X over any other headphone I've heard.

I wanted to like these EL-8's. I truly did. I like the idea of planar magnetics, and Audeze seems like a quality manufacturer based in SoCal. The EL-8's are just surprisingly mediocre. The various raves I read about them online before purchasing make me question the accuracy of a lot of the audiophile press.

Alexa part is interesting but you have to use special phrases to get accurate answers. So instead of expecting an answer when you ask a question you have to say Alexa ask Bing this and that. Silly and flawed. Amazon expects us to buy through Alexa sight unseen, pushing this very hard. Good luck with that, no go with me. As a speaker it's OK sound wise but I wish they would fix time delay on this since when I use it to play spotify from my phone it just turns off as soon as song is finished. If I want to play next song, I have to come to it and turn it on again. Really badly designed to not have time delay after speaker stops working. I understand the need to preserve battery but at the expense of usability??

I consider my purchase bad investment. Simple blootooth speaker would have done what this does and cheaper. If only Alexa part worked at all times and you did not have to come to it and press a button...at least while it's sitting on its charging pad....

I can't really write a fair review of these as I don't think I received a working pair. The right bud never seemed to charge in its case.  I thought I'd figured out that it wasn't being pushed down far enough to make contact and so jury-rigged something that would allow that to happen which seemed to get some sort of charge in it. But I was never able to easily pair with my iPhone, and when I could either the right one died within a few minutes or they disconnected and then wouldn't re-pair.  Best I can say therefore is a) they were comfortable  b) the few minutes of sound I had on scattered attempts sounded better than some of my earbuds but not as good as my PowerBeats 3 or Jabra Elite.

I have to say, I was excited to get this thanks to the zoom for the video, but I was sorely disappointed in its quality. The indoor video I took of my son's music concert, in admittedly relatively low-light (but nowhere near dark) was nearly unwatchable. The focus was terrible and the output was super grainy. My wife, sitting right next to me and thus experiencing the exact same environment, taped the show using our Kodak playsport and it came out absolutely wonderful, well worth sending out to family members. There was simply no comparison between the two. While the sound quality was a closer match, I'd still give the nod to the Kodak over the Phillips. The still photos in the same situation came out just as bad, also grainy, also often blurry, and often washed-out as well. I tried both video and stills at various levels of zoom--without a zoom the quality of both was noticeably better, but still poor quality. I then took stills out in a well-lit hallway and again was disappointed in the quality and again, the Kodak completely outmatched the Phillips.

I've used it in outdoor conditions and better lit conditions and there's no doubt the picture quality is better in those conditions, but in all of them it comes in quite below the Kodak in quality.

Other issues:

The zoom was very slow to auto-focus and took several long seconds before settling in.

the choice of a micro-SD. Not only is it annoyingly different, which I could live with, but it really took some force to get it into the slot. In fact, the first time I used it I left it sticking partway out assuming it was a clever design that shutting the cover would put the card into the slot as it needed to go. This did work--the card obviously slipped in and had no issues--but then, when I needed to connect it to the computer to download, which necessitates leaving the cover open for the cable, I realized what I had thought was a clever design wasn't purposeful, as I needed to get the card all the way in. I eventually used a pen cap to push it in, wincing at the pressure needed to do so. (I won't discuss the times it popped out and I had to search on the floor/desk for it).

it has its pluses, but to be honest, since its primary purpose is taking good pictures and video, and so far it hasn't, I don't see the point in outlining the good points which are so secondary to its primary objective.

I'll use it a few more times to ensure this review is a fair one, but there is no way I will do so at special events or without using the Kodak as backup (or one of my point-and-shoots which also shoot far better video based on the samples so far--two Canon elphs and our larger Canon IS). At this point, not only would I not use this but I wouldn't give it to a friend. But as mentioned, I'll give it a few more chances and report back.

I have only had this TV for 6 months and the remote has died. The remote also went through batteries like they were going out of style. Would not purchase again. I purchased a refurbished TV, but did not expect the remote to die so soon. Very unhappy. As another reviewer said, because there are no buttons on the TV, when the remote dies, you have no options.

Picture and sound are good. I have had no trouble with the apps.

At first. I liked it a lot, I don't really mind the fact that I have to build the approved caller list, but, after few days I discovered that I can t make any outgoing calls with this thing installed. All I get is clicking sound when I try. I tried several phones and none of them worked.
Disappointed.

They just sound horrible, period! No bass whatsoever, none! The midtones are flat. I had my share of cheap headphones, but, these are by far the worst sounding ones. Can't really comment on the comfort because it was painful enough to just listen to these..

I really wanted to like this product. When it worked it has beautifully powerful sound, is unobtrusive and blends in with my decor, and I love the remote.

However, the fatal flaw is dropouts when played from my Dell laptop with Windows 10 using Bluetooth. (Dell Flex 3) The audio will play fine for 1-3 minutes, then drop out (Silent) for 0.5-1 second. The speaker it replaced, a Sony SRSX55 played fine for 4 months. The dropouts do NOT happen with my iPhone or iPad as a source, to which Peachtree support says it MUST be the Dell. Dell support says: nope, we’re fine, it’s the Peachtree. Side note: I also tried it with a Lenovo laptop with Windows 10, and while it was better it still exhibited the same problem.

So I purchased a Marshall WOBURN Bluetooth speaker. It plays flawlessly with Windows 10 and it sounds equally as good as the Deepblue2. (Which it should, since it costs more)

I suspect the Bluetooth section in the Deepblue2 has a poor buffer design. Don’t know for sure, don’t need a project. I returned the Deepblue2 and will keep the WOBURN.

...but I still miss the remote.

Buyer beware! Received one on left with the box already cut open delicately. Internals(usb port and SSD board have been stripped out of the product enclosure. The one on the right is how it's suppose to look. If you look closely the one on the left there is no usb-c port internals. I shined a flashlight in it only to see that it was hollow.

From day 1, whenever I make a call, no one can hear what I'm saying. Instead, they hear a ton of static and a very quiet muffled incoherent voice. Totally useless for communicating. I wish I could return or replace these but now they collect dust in my drawer.
I was disappointed with the sound and returned the speakers. I have the little round "jam" bluetooth speaker also, and I think it sounds better than this one does, but it's not wifi.

Shipping was fast and installation was OK, too - both drivers and ULead. However, capturing from a VCR produced a movie that would have frozen fractions of seconds (or half seconds) every 5-10 seconds. I could actually watch these brief freezes when it was just in the watching mode (i.e. no capturing), which suggests to me that the chipset inside this toy is not keeping up with the amount of video data (voice was OK).
Then, I have found that EasyCap may be just a fake. If you look in the Internet carefully, you will find EZCap - the original device (of course, little more expensive and probably much better) where they explain they used to be called EasyCap, but due to a lot of junk from - you know where - they needed to register their brand as EZCap [[ASIN:B003YGJLWU Ezcap116 USB 2.0 Video Capture Device. Convert video+audio From vhs, V8, Hi8, All Camcorders, Video Recorder, DVD Player, Satellite Tv, Freeview Etc. Capture Xbox360 & Playstation3 in Color. Includes Arcsoft Showbiz 3.5 Editing Software. Output in 16:9 ...]]. They also explain a bit about fake EasyCap devices.
This EasyCap DC60 (it is NOT DC60+) is probably one of those clones...
One star extra goes to Bargain Cable for their nice and responsive customer service - they handled my compliant in a highly professional manner and in a separate review they get 4 stars from me. One less than 5 - for they need to be vigilant and make a little research before they offer junk-performing stuff to the public.

First of these I received from Amazon Warehouse, but all under normal warranty, etc. After paying $60 to install it (and the set of 4 Pioneer speakers in my 2002 Hyundai Santa Fe), I was amazed how it sounds. This radio packs a great deal of features and very decent sound quality into the double-bin box. However, it is made in China, likely without much of a quality control system and it does show it, too... It soon started to trap CD disks and it took sometimes several attempts (button pressing) for it to return them (with a loud noise), then once it simply held one CD forever, even stop reacting to EJECT button.
OK - it is under warranty, I thought, isn't it? Well, yes, but no one tells you you've got to shell out about 35% of the original price for it to be repaired or exchanged. BOSS Audio folks made me pay for my own shipping to California ($10) and demanded $20 to ship it back, thus this was extra $30 paid within warranty anyway.
They apparently gave up with repairing it (cheap stuff) and sent me a new one (along with the CD, retrieved safely from the other one, + for them). I hooked it up myself and now it sounds beautifully. Until it breaks...? Well, I hope not, but the CD does not eject right away - it takes about three button pressings to get it out. Scary, but so far so good. If it does break, I am not sure I'm going to give BOSS another chance for yet an other 30 bucks...
I enjoy this equippment, though, as it sounds very nicely and has good features (plays mp3 disks, has aux input, USB input - beware it accepts maximum 1 GB drives and you may break it if you stick a larger one into it) and decent power (80W). Radio performs well (signal-wise) and sounds great.
If you're lucky then you can have this working for a long time and under $100, but if luck plays the game with you, do not count on the service quality you'd expect from Pioneeer or Sony.
UPDATE at the end of May 2012:
After few months of the new one (replaced) normal use, the unit would not accept CD anymore - it would not even take them in, but it automatically ejects them even if partially inserted. Despite good sound quality, therefore, I am decreasing the ratings to 2 stars because of a terrible (Chinese) build quality.

We bought this to do a tape to tape copy and it was horrible. The sound quality was very washed out and it sounded very bad. I tried to return it but it cost close to $50 to ship the box back due to its size. I tried to ship it without the over box to reduce cost but the return instructions were specific that it had to be protected. So now I am stuck with a system that does not do its job and it is too expensive to return. Bottom line...DO NOT BUY THIS.

Yes, you have to remove the little sticker on the play head before you use it. But this thing still sounds like absolute garbage. Really poor sound quality, as in, not even worthwhile if it was free. Tried it three times, and into the trash it goes.
Bought these in April and now no sound comes out of them. Worked great at first.

I was hopeful with these since I wanted small headphones that still had good sound and mike.  The sound is great.  However, after wearing these for about two hours of Zoom meetings (separated by an hour) I find that my ears hurt. I'm female and would say my ears are normal size--not big or small. We followed the directions over again with no luck. Thankfully we fell within the 90 free tech support window. After troubleshooting with an amazon representative she connected us to a JBL associate who was friendly & arranged for a replacement. She sent an email with the necessary information to receive a replacement. I emailed all this back to her immediately. That was the last I’ve heard of her. Return paperwork was provided & a new speaker was sent.
JBL I do not trust. The Bluetooth had a defect & they failed to resolve it for me. Despite many positive reviews this is my experience. I can only hope the new speaker has longevity. I can not recommend.

I was aware this SONY speaker was refurbished upon purchasing it, obviously a much lower price. I purchased the exact real deal a couple years ago which still work 100% so for my teenage Son I thought I’d go this route.
The speaker looked brand new upon taking it out of the not so much great looking packaging but none the less it was about the speakers. I was impressed. Charged great, connected to his iPhone perfectly. Played the same great quality sound of my speaker. The bass was nice & smooth. No battery or charging issues. My purchase was 5/5/2020. Things were good to go.
That’s the positive piece of my review.
Unfortunately the end of July hit & with the speaker being fully charged it would play for only 45 minutes or less & then it was dead. It would then take a very long time to charge. I decided to contact the seller on 8/4 explaining the speaker was just shy of 3 months old & I’ve already experienced a problem. Their reply?
In 1 sentence they apologized & wrote the return window was 30 days. That’s it. I was shocked. This is the customer service I receive I reply to broken speakers not even 3 months old? Yes it was.
Well I just happened to be looking at my order a little more closer & noticed my return window with amazon was 90 days~their own offering for these types of products. So fortunately I returned the speaker for a full refund.
My 1st refurbished purchase & my last. It’s not worth it for me personally.
Initially these were awesome but the longevity didn’t exist. I was disappointed I didn’t receive support I felt I deserved but amazon was the saver in the end.
I personally don’t recommend these. You’re taking a chance if you purchase. Heads up on the 90 day return window though!

They sent me two replacements and they all have the same problem. The bass buzzes and vibrates. Ryan Adams has too much bass for this speaker. It's pathetic. If I try to play rock or metal forget it, it's completely distorted, unless you turn it down so low that you can barely hear it.
Did not fit in the ear well.  Volume and sound quality were good.  Cord was not up to the standard set by previous Philips in-ear phones I purchased.

I'll start with the good.  And this would have been my review if I had done this earlier.  The sound is great.  Crisp highs, pretty low lows.  Quite comfortable.  Really lightweight.  And also has a removable wire (plug on both ends).  And also a pretty good price.  Everything was leading to a perfect review.  I made up my mind that I should not review anything until after 1 year with the product.  And with these headphones, they never made it.  May 2019 will make a year.  I took my headphones off.  Went to the bathroom.  Came back, put my headphones on.  And the Right side ear-cup broke off.  Now over the year I have dropped my headphones off my desk, 2.5 feet, twice.  But that was 2 or 3 months ago.  And it broke now?  I think somebody skimped out, and chose a cheaper construction material.  Because a lower grade of plastic would save a penny.  They are good headphones, IF you treat them with kid gloves.  I wanted to come back and add to this review, but I forgot all about it.  The depth of the ear-cup on these headphones is unacceptable to me.  My ears are stick out a bit more I guess.  I finally got a (beyerdynamic DT 770 PRO)  It is great.  Think about how many ohms you want.  Because it come in a lot of flavors from 80 to 250.  higher ohm make for deeper base, true.  But you also have to have a bigger amp to drive them.  Or you will have a set of headphones that only go up to 1 decibel.  I have the 80 and they are like others on volume, and nice deep base.  I'm happy.  The Audio-Technica are overpriced and under quality.  For a little bit more money you can be happy with the  beyerdynamic.  And I've dropped them and they hit the floor soft, it the way they are designed.  A hit will cause them to fold in and absorb the shock.  No thud.  If you keep them free of water.  You could give them to your grand-kids.  I got some Marshall stuff from a gramdpa.  Err, I didn't, it was my friend.  This stuff will be good like that.  Marshall had their day, and it is over.  I tried their headphones this year.  I took them back.  Beyerdynamic has the throne for awhile.

I would, that I could give these headphones a zero-star rating. As I don’t think they deserve a whole star. When I was in school, a gold star meant something. And these headphones are not deserving of such.
Ok, on with the bad. My first set of these. If I would whipe the sweat out of my left ear. Left ear specifically, as the right ear did not produce this effect. The sound would cut off. Not the little off, then on again. As the phones shut off when you take them off your head. So a little off then on, would be expected. But I mean off, and stay that way. Then you need to turn off the headphones, with the switch, and back on again.
Which leads to the second problem. The phones cannot reconnect after the connection has been broken. The computer will blue screen, and restart. I thought, well maybe it is the Bluetooth receiver. So I got a new one, by a different company. Same issue.
Problem three. None of the buttons work. The buttons I am referring to are the play, pause, track forward, or track backward.
And it really makes me sad, to say these bad things about these phones. And I really tried to blame something other things at fault, to save their face. Because they have the most awesome form factor I can find in a headphone. The buttons are so intuitively placed, even if they do not work. The design, is obviously a different department. And the volume, is not controlled by a buttons. But rather a good old analog type knob. And the sound quality is pretty good, and also the noise cancelling works.
Oh yeah, I almost forgot. Because I really like the form factor. I thought I should give them another chance. So I replaced this set, with another set of the same model. And had the same problems. Evey, single, one, of them.

After 4 months of careful use, only one speaker works. Apparently the connection of the cord to the headset is flimsy and there was static from day one. But now only one speaker works and that is very irritating.

The moment I opened the package and unfolded the backdrop I knew it was bad work.
Pictures on Amazon show a clean, crisp rendering of a wooden wall that almost looks 3D.
The actual product is out of focus and looks sick.
Even set up to make the backdrop blur in the background it looks bad.
It's just plain bad work.

Two reasons I gave it one star:

First, in order to hear the sound properly while sitting at my desk I actually have to lay it over on its side and point the top of it at me. Simple music comes out fine-ish in its upright position, but if you want to hear words clearly, then you have to point it at you.

Secondly, I actually hate having to power it on, power it off or plug it in to charge - Why? The voice that yells at me "Powering ON! Charging! Powering OFF!" I am replacing it. I might even throw it away so that no one else has to listen to it.

All the versions of Anker’s lightning cables have been a very bad experience for me. I purchased several of these supposedly durable ones and also the regular white ones. No exaggeration: maybe one out of four continue to work. The rest stop working in one way or another eventually. It can’t be that difficult to make a working lightning cable can’t it?!
For sound quality four stars, for WI-FI connection one star. Too many frequently WI-FI disconnected.

Really wanted this to work. And when it does it works OK. It can play a file OK sometimes, but not on other tries. I need something that works more than 20% of the time.

Most of these cameras work OK. When this works, it works reasonable well. My problem is with the mydlink viewing site.
