I returned these. Why? The bass was too prominent (not a balanced bass but punchy) and I could not escape it anywhere in the house. Before this I had Creative Labs Gigaworks speakers that I liked much better. Only reason I switched was sound started cutting out on creative labs. I am getting another set, learned my lesson on Bose, I expected better. Never again.

After using this enclosure for a few months, there is a loud buzzing noise coming out of the ac adapter.
For storing sensitive data in my hard drive, I hoped the item would have better quality parts but this is definitely a you get what you pay for scenario.

I received a defective case.
The volume button on the case did not properly line up to my IPad Pro 9.7.
The magnetic cover did not work; the magnetic was not strong at all.
Workmanship and quality control was poor, there were loose glue.

These are cheap hollow plastic spacers. The second photo clearly shows them to be completely solid spacers. They are not solid. If your speakers mounting holes don’t line up with the pre-existing holes in these cheap spacers they are unusable.
I’ve returned these useless spacers and purchased some spacers which I know to be cut from solid UHMW plastic.

For the first two weeks I thought the Denon AVR3312ci was a great upgrade from my 3 year old Marantz SR7002. Sound quality was very good and the extra power was impressive. The speaker setup (Mythos One mains, Mythos Eight center, Supercube II sub, Mythos Four surrounds, and Mythos Six rears) went well but the manual is very confusing when it comes to manually selecting different sound schemes (e.g. Dolby® TrueHD, DTS-HD(tm) Master Audio, Dolby® Digital Plus, DTS-HD(tm) High Resolution Audio,etc.) Whoever designed the remote needs a remedial class in basic principals of "user friendly" design.

Two days ago I connected the AVR3312ci to a Linksys bridge to enable connection to my home wireless network. That process went very well. Yesterday the receiver started a 40 minute firmware update which, at first, seemed to go well. Video quality immediately after the firmware update was noticeably impaired. Within hours after that the output for both sound and video went completely out. A quick chat with Denon C/S this morning told me the receiver needed repair. Since I live 3 hours from the nearest Denon repair center, it was shipped today to a supercenter repair facility at a cost of $24.

Not sure how many others are having problems with their new $1099 receiver/paperweights but I must say I am really disappointed. It took two hours to pull out the AVR3312ci, put back in the Marantz SR7002 into my HT setup, pack up the AVR-3312ci and get it to FedEx for shipment. I'll update this review as I get more info on what the repair center finds. Right now I can only give it two stars. I can only hope it comes back from repair and works without additional problems!

UPDATE: The Service Center in So Cal did return the "repaired" receiver within 10 days. They did a firmware update checked the output and that was it. After two weeks the same problems returned. Sound would randomly drop out and HD picture quality went horrible after 10-30 minutes of watching when the receiver had warmed up - lots of high contrast ghosts/artifacts that could not be fixed with contrast or any other picture adjustments. Tried turning off HDMI Control function on both TV and receiver per Denon Support to no avail. Additional problems with function of specific remote buttons. If I plug the HDMI directly from the Cable Box or the BluRay player into the TV there are no picture or sound quality problems so I know the problem is within the receiver.

The receiver is back on it's way to Denon's So Cal Service Supercenter (I'm out another $25 in shipping) with a case opened at Denon USA on the problems I'm having. At this point I would say avoid any new Denon receiver. The quality of the product and the quality of support from Denon USA just isn't there.....

SECOND UPDATE: At the repair center for the second time the remote was repaired/replaced, the internal HDMI video board was replaced and the firmware was updated yet again. Returned within 2 weeks from my shipping date. Now, four months later, I can report that the unit has been working just fine. I've very satisfied with the current video and sound quality. But what a hassle to go through to get a new unit to work properly! Starting in December I've been getting another message from the receiver to do a firmware update but frankly I'm now too scared to do it!

LONG TERM UPDATE: Since the HDMI video board and remote control were was replaced I have not had any other issues. Getting great sound and am satisfied with my purchase. I have even successfully completed two firmware updates over the past year. IF YOU DO A FIRMWARE UPDATE YOU MUST USE A HARDWIRED ETHERNET CONNECTION TO THE INTERNET! DO NOT TRY TO USE A WIRELESS BRIDGE OR OTHER WIRELESS TECHNOLOGY TO DO A FIRMWARE UPDATE!!!

I liked this for the year it worked . But now it makes a snap sound and shuts off.
Doesn't work. I read where others have had the same issue.
Been happy with sound quality, but after only 4 months the sound breaks off due to faulty wiring, despite careful use.

I bought 2 pair. (Costco sells them in sets.) The in-line remote stopped working on the first pair after 2 days. It is really delicate and the little push button for stopping/starting/advancing doesn't click/move. If you can use an eq in your application, you might find these headphones surprising. Once the shrill high-end is toned down and the bass and mids bumped up, you will find the sound is pretty good for a ~$60/pair. The soundstage is small, but clear and the instrument separation surpasses what I was expecting. However, boost the bass too much and you will get distortion.

A couple of weeks before buying these I heard the quad-driver version and they were simply amazing. It was like I was sitting in my own living room listening to a full surround sound setup. I've never heard spacial definition or as big a soundstage in a headphone as I did with the quad-drivers, especially IEMs. The quad-drivers are on par with $600/pair HiFiMan planars. That's why I took a chance on this much cheaper bluetooth version of a single driver.

If you don't mind playing with the eq and don't want to buy cheap knock-offs from china (these are made in china, but by the company that designed them), take a chance on these. If you just want to plug and play, buy something else. I'm still on the fence on returning them myself.

I've had a love/hate relationship with Harmony for the past 10 years...but no more second chances.

Just like every Harmony I've ever owned, setup for this required a call to tech support. I'm fairly tech savvy, and this should be easy to set up, but it wasn't. And I know it wasn't me because it took tech support 30+ minutes and 7 syncs to make it function "properly". Yes, "properly" is in quotes because even at its best, it was unimpressive.

On my own using the software, syncing failed to load my activities into the remote. And again...it took tech support 7 syncs to make it work.

Even after it was working "properly", it was still frustrating to use:

1) When switching between TV and SMART TV, it would power the speaker bar on and off. Does Logitech not understand that TV and SMART TV are not 2 separate devices and if you are switching from one to the other the sound should be left on? With a remote this expensive I shouldn't have to dig out the speaker bar remote to turn it back on every time I switch activities.

2) Lack of physical buttons for numbers is annoying. Any time I need the number pad I have to swipe to unlock, then swipe to get to the number pad. Technology is supposed to make processes faster...not slower. And yes, I know I can turn off the lock feature...but then every time I grab the remote it does something I don't want, and that something usually requires time-consuming troubleshooting.

3) As I mentioned before, programming this remote is a nightmare (2+ hours) and even then it couldn't stand alone. I ran into problems only tech support could solve, and even then it took 30 minutes AFTER I had all the correct devices loaded. Please note that this was a simple configuration: Sony smart TV/Fios DVR/Samsung speaker bar. All less than 3 years old. After I returned this remote I bought a "learning" remote and endured programming every single button individually, and it still took a fraction of the time.

4) There is no POWER button. Only an OFF button. You turn things on by selecting an activity. And as stated before...switching to a new activity powers things off that a remote this expensive should understand should be left on. If you are going to have a single OFF button that powers down everything with an activity button that turns everything back on, you should have an ON button for each device so you can quickly turn on any device that for whatever reason doesn't turn on when you fire up the system with an ACTIVITY button. And again...having to do an initial swipe to get to the ACTIVITIES just to turn the system on is annoying. Why does Logitech insist on writing code that slows down the power-on process???

5) You cannot utilize the Harmony software without plugging in the device. Why??? When things aren't working correctly (which is often) we should be able to fire up the app just to review the settings. Then, when you do plug the remote in, you have to wait for the remote and your PC to establish communication. Don't software engineers understand that we HATE waiting for technology to do things? Especially when forced to plug in when we don't want to??? Speaking of plugging in, it is difficult with this remote. First off, there is a totally unnecessary door. That door gets in the way when you're trying to plug in, and plugging in is difficult enough already because the mini-USB port is deeply recessed inside the door. Do we really need to cause all this hassle just to hide a mini-USB port? C'mon Logitech...don't you guys own cell phones? Mini-USB doors are annoying and useless (which is why cell phones stopped using them). Try to keep up.

6) Tech support is only good for 90 days. Based on my experience with this remote and 2 previous Harmony remotes, this means that any changes I make to my very simple home entertainment system will not work, and I will not be able to get help to make them work.

A remote that costs well over $100 should assimilate my entertainment system like the Borg. It should be simple to set up, function extremely quickly/efficiently, and be highly intuitive. This device is just another example of technology that steals away hours of your your life that you will never get back.

I am writing this review because after reading the few reviews available it sounded like this would be a great Media Player. But after receiving the player (a Christmas gift from my wife) I have to wonder if most of the people who reviewed the unit have actually used or even seen one in person. So I reread the reviews and noticed a trend that they don't actually say anything about using the player (all except one).
So here is a real user review.
The good. (I use it for music playback only)
The sound on the player is superb. I rip my cd's using the FLAC format and I have listed to playback using Wired (Grado's) and Bluetooth headphones. I have also listened to it on my home stereo using wired and a Bluetooth connection. There is a slight difference in the tonal quality but in a noisy environment my ears can't tell the difference. Sony digital processor does seem to color the music a little but it is on the warm side so it not objectionable.
I must say I love the sound of this player.
The media program (Media Go) that comes with it is very good for ripping music in any format that the player supports. Setting up playlist to send to the player is a breeze. The program does not have the options of JRiver Media Center but it is simpler to use.
The Bad
It is cheaply built - If feels like a toy. I do not believe it will stand up to daily use. Not a quality product that I have come to expect from Sony. For the price of this unit I expect it to at least have the build quality of my FiiO player or my cassette Walkman (which still works)
Bluetooth- It's a joke. My main reason of wanting this player was Bluetooth connectivity. If you disconnect it from the headphones, stereo -car and home, It take at least three tries for it to reconnect the next time you want to use it and you have to navigate to the Bluetooth screen to do it.
This creates a problem on its own. If you were listening to your playlist and stop at a particular track you now loose that place unless you navigate back to the home screen (more on that later) and bookmark your spot before you try and reconnect to your Bluetooth playback source. This is a major pain.
Screen Navigation. The player has 4 main buttons. The toggle button which surrounds the play and pause button is use for navigation. The navigation is more cumbersome -not user friendly- than it needs to be. Try and navigate while you are working out or somewhere not so well lit and it is frustrating at best. At this price it should have a touch screen. My 29 dollar SanDisk player is easier to use that this setup.
The next problem. You really can't power down the player. Once you power down the player if you accidently touch any button on the player it powers back up. I keep the player in a soft case clipped to my belt. I have bumped the player while in the case and have ended up with a dead battery the next time I wanted to use it.
There are other problems but they are minor and I can live with those.
If Sony wants to play in this market (no pun intended) these major flaws need to be fixed.

I recently purchased this to replace a lost remote for a piece of high end integrated amp. As with most things in the audiophile world, a replacement for this simple 6 button remote was way overpriced ($105) for what it is. So I was pleased to find that my amplifier was supported by the Logitech 650.

My biggest gripe is nearly a dealbreaker. After setting it up I went to use it on my integrated amplifier to raise the volume a little bit. The problem was that I couldn't just give the volume button a quick tap to turn up the volume a little bit. A quick tap of the volume raised the volume a significant amount whereas the original amp controller allowed me to make volume changes in small increments. After some searching I found that I just had to adjust the IR repeat length in the controller setup.

Problem solved, right? Wrong.

First issue was the manual being outdated. The frustration started when I tried following the steps in the manual. The first step was "Click Troubleshoot at the top of the Harmony Remote Software window". The problem was that there was no Troubleshoot button anymore. They had updated the software but didn't update the manual. Eventually I found the new location in the software where you can lower the repeats. The default was set to 1 so I lowered it to 0 (the lowest setting on the 0-4 scale). I saved my changes and after waiting for the remote to update I tried it again and it still was making large volume changes. With the remote already set to the lowest setting the only way I can make small adjustments to volume is to press the volume button and cover the IR emitter on the remote extremely fast so the volume change signal only gets sent out for a quick burst. I'm talking ninja fast. This is extremely annoying and tricky to get the hang of.

PROS
-Price
-Device Compatibility

CONS
-Can't make small volume changes
-Outdated Manual (they updated the software but didn't update the PDF manual with new instructions for the new software). This causes some serious frustration when you are instructed in Step 1 to press a Troubleshooting button that no longer exists.

Final thoughts... I bought this to mainly do one thing. Change volume and input selection on my integrated amp. The inability to change the volume in small increments is a constant annoyance. It should be something that can be fixed with a software or firmware update.

Logitech, please fix this on the software/firmware side.

I returned these because of a software bug with ANC - and also because the call quality was terrible.

These phones stood out for being wireless with active noise cancellation (ANC) AND pass through (so you can hear ambient sounds for safety in the City). Unfortunately, those features are the weak points of the headphones - to the point that I found I would never use the pass through and often didn't bother with the ANC.

SOUND QUALITY: VERY GOOD - EXCEPT - they tend to exaggerate the mid base a little which can make vocals - especially male vocals sound a little unclear. Listening to the same music on speakers vs the headphones, it was just plane more real sounding and pleasant on good speakers. High standard, I know. Other headphones don't have that particular problem (though may have others - like weak bass or sibilant highs). I haven't heard that many competing models, so I don't know how they compare to sennheiser or bose or anyone else in the same price class. At least others have an app with equalization (Jabra, Jaybird).

Bug w. ANC: Sometimes it would say it's on when it's off and vice-versa.

ANNOYING THING: When you engage the pass-through, it has a voice prompt that tells you the pass through is engaged. Since often I switch on the pass through when it's important to hear something, the several seconds it takes to make its silly announcement means I miss part of what I was trying to hear! I found I would always just yank one plug out of my ear instead and get the instant feedback. ALSO - this thing takes FOREVER to turn off. You have to hold hold hold and finally it announces it's powering off. Combined with poor power indicator light - this is just annoying.

NOTE: This is not a defect, but just poor design... There is NO WAY to activate Google Assistant or Siri with These. Even my cheapo earbuds let you use one of the buttons to summon Google. Without that, how are you supposed to make voice calls? I have to pull out my phone to make calls. Foo.

Combined with atrocious call quality (I could hear them, but the person on the other end is always mishearing words or saying WHAT? WHAT?), these are DOA for me.

ONE LAST THING: The APP is garbage. Just pointless.

You can definitely do better for the (low) price.

The HyperDeck Studio Pro is a very specific piece of gear. If you are looking for an HD or UHD/4k player you can put your edited files on and play, think again. It's definitely not an advanced digital Blu-ray or Red-ray player.

The HyperDeck is a recorder. It takes a variety of signals into it (as long as they are standard formats like 720-60p, 1080-60i, etc) and records them as uncompressed QuickTime (gigantic files), Apple ProRes HQ, or two flavors of Avid DNxHD.

It can then play the files back, sort of.

Problems:

1. It will only play back the files if they are all identical formats. If you record a file at 1080-24p, then a file at 1080-29.97/60i, then a file at 720-60p, it will only see the last file recorded and not see the first two at all. They are on the SSD, but not visible by the player. In other words, it cannot switch playback file formats based on the recorded files! You must record all the files in the same format on a formatted SSD.

2. The SSD must be formatted as ExFat (cross-platform PC) or HFS+ (Mac) format, which you must do on a computer as the recorder cannot format the SSDs.

3. The clips are captured with the name "Capture0000.mov", "Capture0001.mov" etc. You can see these names if you mount the SSD in a computer. You cannot see the file names during playback. There is no list of files to choose from on the deck. At best (and if they are all the same format) you can move from file to file using the >>| button. Not a great way to navigate, and you have no confidence what the next file actually is. Seemingly, you can only play the file in the format you last recorded in. For instance, again, if you record in 720p first, then 1080-24p, then 1080-60i, you will only see the 1080-60i file. Very frustrating.

4. The buttons. UGH. They look like the familiar buttons on traditional tape machines like Betacam or DVCAM, but are woefully sad. They light up when pushed, but remain dark when not pushed. This is awful when working in a dim environment. Who wants to have to shine a flashlight on the buttons to see them? Worse, the Record button, when unlit, is the same color (clear unlit plastic) with nothing but the symbol "o" on it. It should be tinted red at least, or have a frame around it or something to make it special. Worse yet, if you press it, by itself, it immediately goes into record. There's no guard around it nor are you required to press "Rec" + "Play" to go into record. And it's right in the middle of all the navigation buttons. Believe me, you will hit it when you least want to, especially in the dark. It won't hurt anything, but you will have an undesired recorded file on the drive that you cannot delete (there's no file delete capability at all, except on a computer). There is no ability to lock an SSD out of record to protect it.

4. Its marketing brochures make it sound like it can play all kinds of files. This leads you to think you can edit a show, render it out, put that on the drive and play it. NOT. There may be a way to render out a show with the precise parameters that the player will see, but I haven't found it. Again, it turns out it's a recorder, period.

This device appears to be designed specifically to record the signal coming out of a camera or a switcher, but you would not know that from the literature or the simply terrible user manual. A call to support will not help much: I got, "Perhaps you can find an answer on the Forums website." Great.

As it has HDMI input (and output), it may be able to record the video signal coming out of a Nikon D800 like the Atomos NINJA 2 does, but I have not proven that yet. This could be useful, though of course the device is strictly 120VAC powered (no battery power input) so you'd need to be near power. And, of course, it's a 1 rack-unit high device that's designed to be installed in a 19" rack, so it's pretty clumsy when sitting loose on a table.

It has some kind of ability to support 4K recording and playback, but trying to figure it out is a dark mystery. We spent the better part of two days messing with our two units and couldn't figure them out. Can it output dual link? Who knows?

Bottom line, if you want to put your show on this machine, you must have the hardware capability to play back your edited show in real time and output via HD-SDI or HDMI, then go into record on the HyperDeck. In that sense, it's more like mastering back to Betacam tape. We fortunately have a Media100 editing system driven by an AJA card that can output in real time via HD-SDI with audio. The three shows we needed to play at an event got onto the machine, eventually. They play back beautifully.

Just don't think you can put the SSD into your computer, copy a file to the SSD and have the player see or play it.

This mini tripod is a pretty good basic design, but to work in practice I had to cut a couple of inches off the center post and swap out the head for a decent ball head. The plastic pan head is simply not strong enough to hold anything but a point and shoot. Certainly not a D800. The head's main problem is the plastic hinge that allows the camera to be rotated into vertical. It's supposed to be an additional feature but makes the head so "floppy" that at best you can only shoot static shots: forget panning or tilting during a video take. It's also very difficult to level the horizon. That hinge again. It simply can't be tightened enough to hold the camera level.

The suction cup on the center post is supposed to attach to a flat surface, but the surface has to be perfect to work. Not likely. The cup deteriorated after a couple of years, too, becoming superfluous. Worse, with the legs retracted to their shortest (and most stable) position the center post has to be extended upwards. Now the camera is really top heavy and, again, the whole thing is unstable.

I speak from trying to shoot video clips in Washington DC, where you aren't allowed to use a full-sized tripod. So I carried this little guy, setting it on domed trash receptacles or benches. Those domes together with That excessively long center post made it almost impossible to use. It wasn't up to the job. I came home and shortened the center post, removed the pan head and replaced it with a sturdy ball head. Still can't really pan, but can at least level the horizon.

I'd recommend a different setup. After I got done cutting the center post and adding a [[ASIN:B000OODPTK Giottos MH1302-655 Professional Calibrated Ball Head with MH 655 Quick Release]] I should have gotten the [[ASIN:B00009UT1V SUNPAK MINI-PROPLUS/B Mini Tripod with Compact Ballhead]].

I knew in 30 seconds these earbuds lacked any low end. No bass at all. The specs say they go down to 12 Hz. Hah. No way. The music is simply not full and rich. The highs are excellent, but with no bass, the music is really thin.

I'm amazed how many reviews say how nice the music is. My throwaway Creative earbuds are much fuller and more sensitive.

With the S3's I have to turn the volume up more and there's still no bass. I would consider this somewhat dangerous. You crank up the volume to get more bass and you burn your ears out with the excessive treble.

I tried all three sizes of earbuds, too, just to see if it was a sealing problem. But no matter which size earbud I tried, the music sucked.

I tried all the EQ settings on my iPhone 4. None added any noticeable bass. Maybe it's an impedance mismatch

This concerns me about other things Klipsch.

I did like the way you can turn them upside down and drape the wires over you ears to hold them in place for running, but I didn't actually try them before putting them away. Might work. Might not. My initial feeling with any of the bud sizes is that they tended to fall out of my ears.

Strangely, the buds that came with an old Creative MP3 player are far superior.

If I had paid the full $49 for these things I would be really upset.

Bought this for the 750 because it didn't come with a case. A similar (smaller) case came with my 360 and I didn't think this purchase through. After using it and comparing the other cases out there, I would buy a different case.

This slipcase for the 750 fits tight. That's good. The Nuvi won't slip out. But because the 750's on/off switch is now a slider on the top left corner, if you slide it into the case naturally (unit in your right hand, case in your left) the switch rubs against the case. When you pull the unit out, it "automatically" turns on. Thus if you were to pull the unit out partially then push it back in, you could turn it on and not know it.

The solution is to invert the Nuvi so its switch will be at the open end of the case after it's in the case. That way you can see the switch's on/off position and verify it's not on.

More practical issues:

Pros:

- Nicely made: very high quality

- Very compact

- Adequate protection against rattling inside a glove compartment or briefcase

- Good basic case

Cons:

- It can accidentally turn the unit on

- It's black: can't find it easily in the dark buried at the bottom of my shoulder bag when traveling. Experienced this with the 360's case. And if it falls on the floor of a rental car at night, good luck trying to find it. Wish it came in natural leather color.

- Offers no protection while hand holding the unit while walking

The [[ASIN:B0012MI7N2 Garmin Nuvi 800 Series Carrying Case]] case is a wallet style that flips open to reveal the screen. It stays on the unit during use and offers some protection if you dropped your Nuvi on the sidewalk while walking. Downside with that unit appears to be that the cover flap does not latch, allowing the case to flip open in a briefcase and the screen to be scratched by other junk. And it's also black and can get lost on a car floor.

Another alternate is one of the many zippered semi-rigid or neoprene cases.

At the time of order the iMito MX1 is the best Android MiniPC available according the FreakTab and the ArmTvTech technical forums. I've put it through my own testing since I received the device 10 days ago and the MX1 did not disappoint.

The Wifi connection just worked. It played 1080p with out any video/audio sync problems. And Installing Apps from the Google Play store was an easy trouble free experience. No upgrade or custom ROMs needed to be installed.

I've connected a 7 port hub to the unit, a usb RJ45 wired Ethernet Dongle, a usb sound card, a 1tb hard drive, a variety of fat32/NTFS formatted thumb drives and several different keyboard/mouse combinations. This all worked in a plug and play manner with no special actions on my part.

The only minor issue I had was inserting a 32gb SD card. It needs to be pressed fairly hard to engage the spring latch to lock the card in place and to remove the memory card. Just a quick note: The Lepai amp is not a particularly good match for these speakers. These speakers can be bright, and the Lepai is a somewhat thin and grainy amp.

============================================
Packaging Construction and Look

(my first set came with bad woofer, and I knocked a star off for that)

They were packed really well. There was a shipping box and then a box in a box to hold the speakers, for 3 boxes total. The speakers are held in nice thick foam with plenty of space between the speakers and the sides of the box. The speakers are wrapped in cloth bags and under the cloth bag is some thin padding. Not sure what use the bags are, except to make them seem like more expensive speakers than they are. To my mind this are over-packed, but better safe than sorry I guess.

At first the appearance seems kind of classy. But after looking at them they start to look kind of plain, make that very plain. I'm ok with the satin/matte, but in the absence of any other kind of styling, not even a logo somewhere, it starts to look like they were sprayed with primer but didn't make it to paint.

They have a fairly nice rubber mat on the bottom and inserts for stand or wall mounting and the quality of the finish is good and they don't look or feel cheap.

I opened up the P4 and looked around, the woofer is a speaker with a Ferrite magnet. While it doesn't really matter to the sound, a Neodymium magnet would be indicative of a more expensive speaker. The specs on the P4 claim 3/4" MDF, but I was able to measure the back and it not even 1/2" thick. What they call "heavily braced" is actually MDF laminated together to get the thickness needed to mount the speakers and I'm assuming where the lamination is equals 3/4". I could not evaluate the thickness of the sides, But if I had to guess from tapping/knocking on them I'd say it's the same thinner material. The speaker connectors are good quality taking bare wire or a banana jack, and are angled in such a way that the speaker can be put very close to a wall.

===============================================

Background

These are the 3rd set of speakers I've auditioned in 3 weeks in the $150 to $250 price range in the same computer based system. Amplification was the Topping TP30 (which I recommend very highly)

Sound source was mostly ogg/Mp3 music rips between 192kbs - 320kbs of my CD's and some, but not a lot of FLAC. Casual listening was mostly a 300 song playlist on grooveshark of songs recommended by people for speaker auditioning. Other listening was 320kbs streams from Spotify and 192kbs streams from Pandora.

All listening was from computer desk distances in a small 10x12 room.

In a past life I made my living for 5+ years dong live sound/stage work and some studio mix down work. I play acoustic guitar for my own enjoyment, and work on electric guitars as a hobby and for friends. I have been using some of my speaker test songs for 20+ years and listening to some of them for 30+.

===============================================

Updated 2/16/2014 after ~2 weeks of listening

Sound review

Note: People who really want to understand these speakers, and their problems, should read the review at noaudiophile.

I can see why people like these speakers, but I can't like them enough to keep them.

There is something going on in the midrange on the P4s that is not right. Male vocals hit a certain frequency and it loses something. It loses some of the 'chest' sound. Female vocals can start to sound harsh. Certain notes on an acoustic piano take on a artificial 'plinky' sound. Snare drums have too much 'crack' and not enough 'pop' if that makes sense. Guitar strings can be a bit jangly.

This all matches up to the review at noaudiophile.

This doesn't mean they sound horrible, it just means they don't sound right all the time. They do bass well. It's punchy and you start rocking out in your seat and it's well controlled and defined. (I have listened to them with and without a sub)

Depending on the music/instrumentation they can have a very pleasing sound, if at times a touch bright, but sibilance is always under control.

After 2 weeks I have noticed a disconnect between the Woofer and Tweeter. This also matches the review at noaudiophile (which has graphs to show the hole in the frequency response)

This bothers me, because this speakers are expensive for what they are, there shouldn't be a 'hole' in the frequency response causing the problems above.

They are forgiving of placement, including height. Mine ended up next to my 24" monitor with the top of the speakers about eye level and the speakers pointing straight ahead. Stereo imaging is only Ok and the do not have a strong center image, which is part of the reason my speakers ended up being placed near my monitor. This would probably improve if I toed them in, but having them pointed straight sounded better to me.

=============================

Conclusion

In spite of the above:

Most people will like how these speakers sound, even picky me could get used to them (well except for the disconnect between the woofer and tweeter, that still bugs me).

But the value isn't there for me, not with a big hole in the frequency response. Steven Guttenberg can gush over these all he wants but the hole in the frequency response is there and the review at noaudiphile shows it's there. How much or how little this bothers you depends on you, how well you know your music, what other sound systems you listen on, etc.

With the Topping Amp (the best value in an amp with a DAC) you are now in budget of $335 dollars.

For out and out sound, I'd give them 4 stars, but that is out of respect to the good reviews that are out there for these speakers. I took star off for the bad speaker out of the box (there is no excuse for that given what these cost vs cost to make), and took 1 star off for the lack of value for the price.

========================================

Final thoughts

I think the Behringer MS40 a similar size speaker is worth a hard look (the MS40 is one of the speakers I auditioned in the last month). For $100 less you get an amp, a DAC, two inputs, one digital, independent volume control of the two sources, tone controls on the front and a headphone jack.

Unlike the P4 the Behringer the MS40 is a great deal for the money. Based on the sound, I'd have to give it to the P4s for being slightly more musical sounding, while the MS40 has a more 'studio monitor' sound but can be a bit muddy, in an area where the P4 sounds very good.

In the same size class, while I haven't heard them but based on reviews, I'd also give the M-Audio AV 40 some serious consideration.

The Behringer and M-Audio show it is not that expensive to put 4 speakers in a box and have it sound good. And Behringer and M-Audio manage to get you an amp in the deal, and for a lot less money.

Another example of what 'what-you-get' for your money, and another option, take a look (not on Amazon) is the Swan M50W. For $50 more than the P4, (less if you consider the cost of the Topping amp), you get an active 2.1 system with a seriously attractive finish and a very sexy volume puck from a Manufacture of some very high-end speaker systems.

These speakers were OK for a while, then started to go in and out. I have them attached to my desktop computer. After a while I just stopped using them because I have my computer hooked up to my HD Roku TV as a monitor, so I use the speakers in the TV for my computer sound now.
This did not do what they said it would.  I heard cracks and pops and the sound was uneven. I sent it back.

I really wanted to like these. They have an interesting design and the idea of being able to sleep comfortably with these in your ears intrigued me.

Unfortunately, they are just not good. The sound is very basic, tinny without any detectable bass.
Also, the voice that declares the status of the device is in what sounds like Chinese. I was unable to determine how to change the language, or if it's even possible.

You also better keep up with the charge cable that comes with these because I was only able to find one other cable in my whole house that would work to charge them.

As I said, I love the look. The digital charge indicator on the case has a really nice aesthetic.
I just can't recommend that you spend your money on them when much better earbuds can be found at this price point.

If I had written this review 2 years ago, I would have given the player 3 or 4 stars. It played the couple Blu-ray disks I had (or which I had gotten from Netflix) and it interfaced really nicely with my Samsung TV.

But I'm writing this in January 2013. After I had returned two sets of Harry Potter Blu-ray disks to Amazon complaining that they must be defective. Since my Samsung played my "Blade Runner" Blu-ray just fine, it *MUST* have been those disks, right? Well, maybe not. I also rented several Blu-rays from Red Box - and none of them seemed to play. I either get pixelation, freezes, and audio issues several minutes in - or the disk doesn't play at all and I get the message "This disc can not be played". Yes - I did update to the latest firmware and tried again.

My advice - stay away from this player. I noticed that Amazon no longer sells it itself, but just in case you're considering it from another seller, be warned.

I bought this tablet as a gift for my mom for x-mas. Although my wife and I have been *very* happy with our Apple iPad, I couldn't bring myself to spend $499 for a gift that I wasn't even sure my mom was going to use. In retrospect, I should have spent the extra money.

On the surface, the Kindle Fire HD 8.9" has a lot going for it: great speakers (but not really loud enough!), excellent wi-fi reception, and a screen that is very nice, indeed. In general (more on that later), performance is good also and overall build quality seems excellent - I'd say on par with the iPad.

So what is the problem?

Well, it all boils down to poor usability. At least for people who are not technologically inclined or those who don't have good hand/eye coordination. Let me explain by way of my experiences trying to teach my mom how to use the device:

The first stumbling block for my mom was finding the power and volume buttons. They are the same black color as the tablet and don't stick out much. They are difficult, especially with pudgy fingers, to find easily.

The second problem involves a GUI principle known as "discoverability". Quite a few very common functions on the Fire HD are not visible at all - the user has to simply "know" the gesture that brings them forth. The primary example I speak of is the "Settings" & brightness adjustment. You'd think that something like "Settings" would deserve a button somewhere on the user interface, but the Amazon GUI designers didn't think so. They thought that it is instinctively intuitive to swipe down from the top of the screen to expose a menu that has a brightness slider and something mysteriously labeled "More..." - well, that "More..." turns out to be the "Settings". And, no, my mom did not instinctively know where to swipe to get to these primary functions.

The next problem involves the tablet's lack of flexibility in terms of catering to the visually- or motor-impaired. My mom had a stroke a year ago and although she's fine, her hand-eye coordination is slightly impaired. Enough so, that she had a lot of trouble with two primary navigation icons on the Fire HD: the "Home" (picture of a house) and "Back" (a left arrow) buttons. These buttons are quite small and very close to one another. My mom, unless she was very careful, would sometimes hit one versus the other. Unlike the iPad, the Amazon Fire HD has ABSOLUTELY NO ACCESSIBILTY settings to help out with this sort of thing. Common, Amazon, there was absolutely no reason to make those icons so small AND so close to one another. That's just stupid UI design (I know whereof I speak - I'm a GUI software developer).

Then we ran into the problem of the tablet getting slower over time - the carousels that Amazon was so fond of and designed a whole GUI with them no longer moved smoothly; menus took a second or two to popup, pages on books no longer flipped effortlessly. I suspected an app we had started was causing a problem (I think it was Skype), but I had the hardest time finding the place to kill running applications. I don't remember exactly how long it took, but it must have been 10-20 minutes. It shouldn't be that hard to kill off running applications! By contrast, on all iOS devices, you get to your running apps by double-tapping the Home button. Maybe Android has a standard too, but since Amazon completely "redesigned" the user interface of Android, that wouldn't have mattered.

Finally, there are the applications - or, should I say, the lack of applications. Amazon does not let its Fire HD users access the Google Play store and its hundreds of thousands of apps. Instead, they get the Amazon store - with not many of the most useful apps. Most notably, I did not see any replacement browsers for the horribly slow one that Amazon put on its Fire tablets ("Silk" is anything but silky smooth). I don't even recall finding Google apps (but I have to admit to not having spent a lot of time in the Amazon store, searching).

All, in all, I think the Amazon Fire HD 8.9" is a pretty limited device for a limited set of users. It is nowhere near as functional and as useful as an iPad. I hate to say it, given how much a fan of Amazon and the Kindle e-readers I am, but I wish I had not been so cheap and gotten my parents an iPad. There is a reason those tablets are becoming the defacto standard in schools, rehabilitation centers, etc. They're fool proof and have a GUI anybody can understand.

Arrived without set-up or quick set up instructions.  Got it to work on occasion.  Sound is great but not constant.  Got lots of offers of help from Amazon, but in the long run got screwed for return shipping charges (partly my fault -- lack of knowledge on return policy).  I have always loved being able to find what I want on Amazon, but returning is a real hassle, problems are a hassle, getting to discuss the problem is a hassle.  I am learning to shop local.

One of the few headsets that has no volume control.  This alone disqualifies the headset.  The mic quality is actually decent and as a spare headset for travel, this may be an OK option - but not a default option.  There is no active noise cancellation (obviously), may block some noise - but on an airplane system, this didnt give enough volume or noise blocking to be useful in airplane entertainment systems either.  Not worth taking a chance on this model.

A device like this is only really any good if you have it with you when you need it, and if people haven't grown so accustomed to the sound that they stop paying attention to it.

As such, I can't really recommend this product. It hangs from the trigger pin so that it can be easily grabbed and pulled when needed. The problem is that the device is so hefty and the pin so sensitive that it will frequently go off just from being jostled a bit while walking. In fact it goes off so easily that you are more likely to just leave it home rather than deal with the constant embarrassment and hassle, and others are likely to start ignoring the sound if they hear it often enough. This makes it pretty ineffective for its intended use.

It gets two stars from me, because it's pretty loud which is what it's meant to be, but otherwise the design is lacking.

I purchased this lens for use as a lower-cost telephoto for bird and wildlife photography. I had heard good things about the sharpness and image stabilization of this lens, although the focus speed was not said to be fantastic. I had not had great results from Tamron lenses in the past, but the word was that they had improved dramatically and that this lens was a great deal. I figured I would give it a shot.

The first lens I got, new from a reputable vendor, was simply defective. The images were very soft and there was no range in which objects were in focus; everything from close to far was blurry. I returned it to the vendor for replacement.

The replacement was not as terrible as the first, but it was still soft and had weird specular highlights, for lack of a better way to describe it. The glass elements clearly caused some distortion of the light, which became even more obvious when the images were cropped. The images were "passable" for someone who never crops and never prints large, but they were nowhere near as good as I had expected.

The image stabilization is really very good, at least on stationary objects, although it uses up battery life rapidly. When I switched it to the mode for following moving objects, it did not perform as well, but perhaps this is due more to the lens' slow autofocus. The autofocus is noisy and sounds more like an industrial machine rather than a piece of performance equipment, and it can not keep up with moving objects. It does even worse in less-than-stellar lighting.

In the end I exchanged the replacement Tamron lens for a Canon 100-400mm, and when compared side-by-side at full zoom the images from the Canon 100-400 far exceed the quality from the Tamron 150-600. Although it costs a bit more and it doesn't have as much reach, I feel that the extra reach is wasted if the images are so soft that the detail is lost. Also, the Canon lens, while still hefty, is substantially lighter, and the autofocus is much faster and quieter. It also can focus much closer, making it more useful for macro photography, and its image stabilization is excellent. Also, despite being lighter in weight, the Canon actually feels more solidly built.

The image below shows a side-by-side comparison of the moon taken with the replacement Tamron (not the defective one) and the Canon lens I finally settled on. These images were taken in the exact same circumstances a few days apart (which accounts for the change in the moon's phase appearance). More details are visible, and sharper, with the Canon lens, despite it maxing out at 400mm rather than 600mm.

Initially I would give these five stars, however they stopped working after 6 months. No sound at all. I really liked them as I have small ear holes and they fit very well, but a 5 month life is not acceptable.

I’ll start with the pros. The headband is super soft. I love the feel of it and the headphones are very flat which is nice if your a side sleeper. I found the headband to have plenty of stretch and to be very lightweight. I also did not find it to be hot at all.
However, I bought this to watch movies in bed without disturbing my hubby and the volume simply is not loud enough. I have it turned up all the way and can barely hear what I am watching. Once you do get to maximum volume the headphones emit an EXTREMELY LOUD BEEP. It startles you and makes me wonder if the beep can be that loud why on earth are the headphones so quiet? They are obviously capable of being much louder.
I admit I have not used these for sleeping. If your purpose is to listen to quiet music, a sleep story, or sleep sounds I think the volume will work perfectly for you. If your purpose is to watch movies or listen to music while you work out, these will not do the trick. They are simply too quiet.

I’m pretty disappointed in this. I used to have a laptop cooler that was amazing and would leave my laptop cool to the touch as I was using it, but it died quite a while ago. Ever since it stopped working, I have wanted to get a replacement. I found this one and decided to give it a try. It looks nice and is lightweight, but it doesn’t do much at all to cool down my laptop. My laptop is still very warm while using this on the highest setting. There’s little grips on the top that are supposed to help stop your laptop from sliding around and they keep popping off and I have to keep sticking them back down which is a little annoying as well. I guess if nothing else, this keeps the laptop off of my lap so my legs don’t warm up when using it, I just wish it was better at actually cooling down my laptop.

This is a replica of the X Mini II, and not the real thing. If I were you, I'd ask any sellers of X-Minis if they are selling the genuine item, complete with original packaging (google it to see what it looks like). A carrying case should be included, too. This item was from China, and had very plain, generic packaging and instructions, with no reference to X-Mini II (probably due to copyright and trademark violations). The item itself looks exactly like an X-Mini, but the sound quality was very distorted at higher volume on the phone and computer.

It functions, I'll give it that. I'd consider it the lowest quility 1080p webcam I've come across. It says 1440p on the box (not the listing) and, in retrospect, that as a joke is of higher quality than the product itself. The picture is muddy and responds horribly to any lighting. I'd look elsewhere for a webcam.

I have really mixed feeling about this device. When I first pulled it out of the package I was ready to give it five stars. I tried it with my OnePlus 9 Pro and it worked perfectly. The sound quality was great, the cable seemed well made with a nice braided sheet on the outside. It's nice and flexible. The problem came when I went to plug it into a Galaxy S20 for which this was specifically purchased and which is specifically supported in the item description. I was immediately greeted with a USB device not supported message.

I tried rebooting and then the other cable. I know some of these have built in DACs and some are able to pull audio straight from the USB connection in the phone. I don't know which method my phone needs, but frankly I don't care. If you say your product supports my phone and it doesn't, you have a defective product.

These work in that they allow you to connect a pair of wired headphones to a phone without a headphone jack. Unfortunately, that's where it ends. The onboard DAC is garbage. It sounds terrible and has low level background static noise whenever sound is coming from the phone. This is most obvious when you are navigating your device with the little clicks as you select different menu items. Every time you touch the screen you get a tiny little burst of 'shhhhh' static. This is going to go straight in the garbage as it's not work the hassle of returning. Don't waste your money or your time.

I really really wanted to like these. I got them to keep a spare set of earbuds in my car for when I forget to take my airpod pros with me or when I don't want to risk losing those. I wasn't expecting or needing the sound quality to be as high; I would've been perfectly happy with the sound and noise cancellation of these if I didn't have other issues.

Regardless of which tips I use, I could not get the earbuds to sit comfortably in my ears. They always felt like they were going to come out, and I found that if a laughed/crinkled my eyes, they would actually come out. I also wasn't crazy about how touching the round part turned them on/off. When I'd be fiddlng with them trying to get the fit right, I'd be constantly turning them off and on. I prefer the design of touching the stem to turn on/off where it's a mre deliberate act.

Other than that, bluetooth pairing was straightforward as was charging and seeing how much charge was left in the case. As far as I can tell, there's no way to know how much each individual bud is charged which is disappointing. I looked everywhere for a label of left vs right when out of the case and couldn't find anything until I saw in the maual that they're supposed to be labeled and I looked again. The R and L are super tiny and hard to read such that they're not usable in most lighting situations.

Overall, these were a bust for me. I'd opt for my wired earbuds as a backup pair over these.
The headphones with the volume adjuster has already broke after 3 uses. Would not recommend!

I really wanted to like these! But, sound quality was horrible. People on the phone call could not hear me then when adjusting the volume with the bud in ear was hard to do. It wouldn't respond to touch very well and when it did was at a time when you didn't want it too. My hair brushed up against it and it would respond to my hair not my finger. I returned it and will hopefully find something else that works with my needs.

The sound was incredible! I ordered one pair. Returned them in exchange for another pair of the same product. Both pairs had the same issues that made them impossible. They’re really uncomfortable. You have to keep pushing them into your ear canal because they slide out. After a few days, the right stops pairing with the left which means that only one bud works. Too bad.
It does make a sound when door or window open but they do not stick very well. We cleaned the area and made sure it was dry. It wouldn’t stick keeps falling down. :(

Battery charges fast, transparency is very good. However, the touch screen options not too sure yet. Also, I have not tried the water resistant part as well...as of today, I ha e noticed that the sound is not consistent... Rumbling and not clear considering how much they cost..

I returned this item after trying it out for a few days. The construction quality of the item is good, but the optics are not up to par. There is quite a lot of optical distortion at all levels and, when zoomed, I can't get the thing focused clearly. I was very disappointed. I spent more and got the Nikon Eagleview and really like it. It's much much better.

I was excited to see how easy it was to record, however, there was no sound on the recording, no sound in the mp3 files, and no sound when I just tried to play the cassette. I played the cassette on another recorder and I could hear it clearly.

Sound is great... but the foam pads consistently come off since the first use.
I only use them when my grandkids are in town... so kind of too late to return.
Batteries are a little hard to change.

I had a problem with the optic connection on one of my televisions. While it works fine on one of them, the other just produced a loud squealing noise. Recently, I bought these headphones because I wanted the full experience for music with a touch of Deep-bass in any song in my personal music Library. Unfortunately, these so-called HD headphones did not deliver on what I wanted in a pair of full-cup headphones. Each time I wanted to listen to songs with a deep-bass pulse, it skips in the sound quality output because of the extensive cord. That's not what I wanted in a pair of awesome headphones. But yeah, it works on some songs, but not all of them. But the best parts of this product is that it is very comfortable, very relaxed and keeps your ears warm...with the power of music, that is. :D

This is much smaller than I thought and does not have the best bass in the music. My husband says he likes it but he may just be being kind. If your looking for a more realistic sound I suggest you keep looking.
The plus is it is cute.

I had to cut a lot of holes wider for it to fit on my Yukon 2004 for a BOSS AUDIO BV9372BI. It's very cheap fragile plastic and it doesn't set nicely around the edges. You see an open gap on the bottom of your stereo, but what can we do? I think this is the only place where you can get it.

In the pictures it doesn’t look as bulky as it is. Not a great fit. Can’t return for full refund only partial. Now I’m stuck with a product I can’t use comfortably. Sound comes and goes when listening to music. Also you can’t talk with it, people can’t hear you or they hear echoes.
